proposals.title: NIT Logistics: Automated Carrier Onboarding & Invoice Reconciliation Platform

intake_data.client_needs_summary: Manual carrier onboarding and delayed invoice reconciliation causing 25 hours/week of overhead.
intake_data.project_scope: Automated carrier onboarding workflow, invoice OCR reconciliation, and an executive KPI dashboard.
intake_data.target_roles: Recruitment Ops Consulting, Workflow Automation, Supabase Architecture
intake_data.constraints: Must integrate with existing ERP via REST APIs. SOC 2 Type II compliance required.

sections.introduction: NIT Logistics currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating significant operational overhead and introducing reconciliation delays that impact cash flow visibility. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design and implement an automated carrier onboarding workflow, invoice OCR-based reconciliation system, and executive KPI dashboard. The solution will integrate seamlessly with NIT Logistics' existing ERP infrastructure via REST APIs while maintaining SOC 2 Type II compliance. By automating these critical processes, NIT Logistics will reclaim operational capacity, reduce invoice processing cycle time, and gain real-time visibility into carrier performance and financial metrics.
sections.project_scope: NIT Logistics' current operational model relies on manual data entry and document processing for carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation. This manual approach creates three primary pain points: (1) Carrier onboarding requires duplicate data entry across multiple systems, consuming 12–15 hours weekly; (2) Invoice reconciliation via manual PDF review and spreadsheet matching introduces 8–10 hours of weekly overhead and creates reconciliation delays; (3) Executive visibility into carrier performance and financial KPIs is limited to static monthly reports. The proposed engagement will address these constraints through three integrated workstreams: Automated Carrier Onboarding Workflow (capturing carrier data once, validating against compliance requirements, and auto-provisioning in downstream systems); Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine (extracting invoice line items via optical character recognition, matching against purchase orders and receipts, and flagging discrepancies for human review); and Executive KPI Dashboard (real-time visualization of carrier performance, invoice aging, reconciliation status, and cost analytics). The solution must integrate with NIT Logistics' existing ERP via REST APIs, enforce SOC 2 Type II compliance controls, and operate within a fixed 8-week delivery window across three phases. Out-of-scope items include: custom ERP modifications, carrier communication platform development, and multi-tenant SaaS productization.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute this engagement using a phased, API-first architecture built on Supabase (PostgreSQL backend with real-time capabilities) and modern workflow automation patterns. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) will focus on Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design: conducting detailed discovery sessions with NIT Logistics operations and finance teams to map current carrier onboarding and invoice workflows; documenting ERP API specifications and authentication mechanisms; designing the data schema for carrier profiles, invoices, and reconciliation records; and producing a detailed technical architecture document and compliance roadmap. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6) will deliver Core Platform Development: building the Supabase backend with carrier onboarding tables, invoice storage, and reconciliation logic; implementing OCR integration (via a third-party OCR provider such as Tesseract or AWS Textract) to extract invoice line items; developing REST API endpoints to sync carrier and invoice data bidirectionally with the ERP; building the executive KPI dashboard using a modern frontend framework (React or Vue.js) with real-time data bindings; and implementing SOC 2 Type II controls including audit logging, role-based access control (RBAC), encryption at rest and in transit, and data retention policies. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8) will encompass Testing, Compliance Validation & Go-Live: executing end-to-end integration testing with the ERP; conducting security and compliance audits to validate SOC 2 Type II readiness; performing user acceptance testing (UAT) with NIT Logistics operations and finance teams; deploying to production; and delivering comprehensive documentation and training. Throughout the engagement, Koya Talent will employ Agile sprint ceremonies (weekly standups, bi-weekly demos, and retrospectives) to maintain transparency and adapt to emerging requirements.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs across the three phases: (1) Technical Architecture & Compliance Design Document (Phase 1): detailed system architecture diagrams, data schema specifications, ERP API integration patterns, and SOC 2 Type II compliance control matrix; (2) Carrier Onboarding Workflow Module (Phase 2): fully functional web application enabling carrier data capture, validation against compliance rules, and auto-provisioning to the ERP; (3) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine (Phase 2): backend service integrating OCR technology, invoice line-item extraction, PO matching logic, and discrepancy flagging; (4) Executive KPI Dashboard (Phase 2): real-time web dashboard displaying carrier performance metrics, invoice aging reports, reconciliation status, and cost analytics with drill-down capabilities; (5) REST API Layer (Phase 2): documented, production-ready API endpoints for bidirectional ERP synchronization, including authentication, rate limiting, and error handling; (6) SOC 2 Type II Compliance Package (Phase 3): audit logs, access control policies, encryption certificates, data retention procedures, and incident response playbook; (7) End-to-End Testing Report (Phase 3): integration test results, security audit findings, UAT sign-off documentation, and production readiness checklist; (8) Deployment & Runbook Documentation (Phase 3): step-by-step deployment guide, operational runbook, troubleshooting guide, and 24-hour post-launch support; (9) User Training & Knowledge Transfer (Phase 3): recorded training sessions for operations and finance teams, user guides, and administrator documentation. Koya Talent will assign a dedicated Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect as engagement lead, supported by a Senior Backend Engineer (Supabase/PostgreSQL), a Full-Stack Developer (frontend & API integration), and a Security & Compliance Specialist.
sections.timeline: The engagement will execute across 8 weeks in three delivery phases with the following milestones: Phase 1 – Requirements & Architecture (Weeks 1–2): Week 1 includes kickoff meeting, discovery sessions with operations and finance stakeholders, and ERP API documentation review; Week 2 includes architecture design completion, data schema finalization, and compliance roadmap sign-off. Phase 2 – Core Development (Weeks 3–6): Week 3 includes Supabase backend setup, carrier onboarding module scaffolding, and OCR integration planning; Week 4 includes carrier onboarding module completion, invoice OCR engine development, and initial ERP API integration; Week 5 includes executive KPI dashboard development, advanced reconciliation logic, and internal testing; Week 6 includes API refinement, dashboard optimization, and UAT environment setup. Phase 3 – Testing, Compliance & Go-Live (Weeks 7–8): Week 7 includes end-to-end integration testing, security audit, SOC 2 Type II validation, and UAT execution with NIT Logistics team; Week 8 includes UAT sign-off, production deployment, post-launch monitoring, and knowledge transfer completion. Critical milestones include: Architecture Sign-Off (end of Week 2), Carrier Onboarding Module Ready for UAT (end of Week 4), Executive Dashboard Ready for UAT (end of Week 5), Production Go-Live (end of Week 8). All deliverables will be tracked via weekly status reports and bi-weekly steering committee meetings with NIT Logistics leadership.
sections.pricing: Koya Talent proposes a fixed milestone-based fee structure of $48,000 for the complete 8-week engagement. This fee encompasses all labor, architecture design, development, testing, compliance validation, and knowledge transfer as outlined in the Deliverables section. The fee is structured as follows: Phase 1 Completion (Requirements & Architecture) – 25% ($12,000) due upon architecture sign-off at end of Week 2; Phase 2 Completion (Core Development) – 50% ($24,000) due upon UAT environment readiness and dashboard/OCR module completion at end of Week 6; Phase 3 Completion (Testing, Compliance & Go-Live) – 25% ($12,000) due upon production go-live and knowledge transfer completion at end of Week 8. This fixed fee assumes the scope remains as defined in the Project Scope section and that NIT Logistics provides timely access to ERP systems, API documentation, and key stakeholders for discovery and UAT sessions. Out-of-scope change requests (e.g., additional dashboard modules, custom ERP modifications, or extended support beyond Week 8) will be quoted separately on a time-and-materials basis at [TO BE CONFIRMED] hourly rates. The engagement does not include ongoing managed services, SLA-backed support, or infrastructure hosting costs; NIT Logistics is responsible for Supabase instance provisioning and hosting (estimated at [TO BE CONFIRMED] monthly based on usage). Travel and expenses are included in the fixed fee for up to two in-person discovery/UAT sessions; additional travel will be reimbursed at cost.
sections.next_steps: To proceed with this engagement, Koya Talent and NIT Logistics must complete the following actions: (1) Proposal Review & Sign-Off: NIT Logistics leadership (John Doe and relevant stakeholders) will review this proposal and confirm acceptance of scope, timeline, and pricing by [TO BE CONFIRMED]; (2) Master Service Agreement (MSA) Execution: Koya Talent will provide a standard MSA and Statement of Work (SOW) for legal review and execution by both parties; (3) Kickoff Meeting Scheduling: Upon MSA execution, Koya Talent's engagement lead will schedule a kickoff meeting with NIT Logistics' operations, finance, and IT leadership to confirm discovery session participants and ERP access requirements; (4) ERP Documentation Handover: NIT Logistics will provide API documentation, authentication credentials (in a secure vault), and current system architecture diagrams to Koya Talent's technical team; (5) Engagement Commencement: Phase 1 discovery and architecture work will commence on [TO BE CONFIRMED] with the first weekly standup scheduled for [TO BE CONFIRMED]. For questions, clarifications, or to schedule a pre-engagement alignment call, please contact Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) at [TO BE CONFIRMED] or John Doe (NIT Logistics) at adedamolaadejumo484@gmail.com. Koya Talent is committed to delivering a transformative automation platform that will reclaim 25+ hours of weekly operational capacity and provide NIT Logistics with real-time financial and operational visibility.

proposals.title: FIRMA Employee Salary Payment Optimization Engagement

intake_data.client_needs_summary: Testing how we can improve payment of employee salary

sections.introduction: Koya Talent is pleased to propose a comprehensive engagement with FIRMA to assess, design, and optimize your employee salary payment processes. This three-month engagement will evaluate current payment workflows, identify operational bottlenecks, and implement targeted improvements to enhance efficiency, compliance, and employee satisfaction. Our Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect will lead discovery and design activities in partnership with your internal stakeholders to ensure recommendations are practical, scalable, and aligned with your enterprise governance standards.
sections.project_scope: This engagement focuses on the end-to-end employee salary payment lifecycle at FIRMA. The scope includes: (1) Current-state assessment of salary payment processes, systems, and controls; (2) Identification of pain points, delays, compliance gaps, and manual touchpoints; (3) Benchmarking against industry best practices and standard enterprise guidelines; (4) Design of an optimized salary payment workflow incorporating automation, error reduction, and audit trails; (5) Evaluation of technology enablers (payroll systems, banking integrations, reporting tools) to support improved payment velocity and accuracy. The engagement explicitly excludes: custom software development, permanent staffing, or changes to compensation policy or employee contracts. Deliverables will be recommendations and design artifacts; implementation execution is out of scope unless separately contracted.
sections.recommended_approach: Our engagement will follow a structured four-phase methodology: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Discovery & Current-State Analysis – Conduct stakeholder interviews with HR, Finance, Payroll, and IT teams; document existing salary payment workflows, system dependencies, and pain points; review compliance requirements and audit controls. Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Gap Analysis & Benchmarking – Compare FIRMA's processes against industry standards and regulatory requirements; identify root causes of delays or errors; assess technology readiness and integration capabilities. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–10): Design & Recommendations – Develop optimized workflow designs; propose technology enhancements or integrations; create implementation roadmap with phased milestones; define success metrics and KPIs. Phase 4 (Weeks 11–12): Validation & Handoff – Present findings and recommendations to leadership; conduct knowledge transfer sessions with your operations team; provide documentation and change management guidance. Throughout, we will maintain alignment with your enterprise governance standards and ensure all recommendations are operationally feasible and cost-justified.
sections.deliverables: 1. Current-State Process Documentation – Detailed flowcharts, system diagrams, and narrative descriptions of existing salary payment workflows, including all manual steps, system touchpoints, and control procedures. 2. Pain Point & Gap Analysis Report – Executive summary identifying bottlenecks, compliance risks, error patterns, and opportunities for improvement, with root-cause analysis. 3. Industry Benchmark Report – Comparative analysis of FIRMA's salary payment practices against peer organizations and best practices, highlighting performance gaps and leading practices. 4. Optimized Workflow Design – Proposed end-to-end salary payment process incorporating automation, error controls, audit trails, and compliance checkpoints; includes process flowcharts and detailed procedure documentation. 5. Technology Assessment & Recommendations – Evaluation of current payroll systems, banking integrations, and reporting tools; recommendations for system enhancements, integrations, or replacements with cost-benefit analysis. 6. Implementation Roadmap – Phased implementation plan with milestones, resource requirements, risk mitigation strategies, and success metrics for rolling out optimized processes. 7. Knowledge Transfer & Training Materials – Documentation, process guides, and facilitated training sessions to enable your team to sustain and evolve the optimized processes. 8. Executive Presentation – Final presentation to FIRMA leadership summarizing findings, recommendations, and business case for improvements.
sections.timeline: Phase 1 – Discovery & Current-State Analysis: Weeks 1–3 (September 18 – October 2, 2026). Deliverables: Process documentation, stakeholder interview summaries, system inventory. Phase 2 – Gap Analysis & Benchmarking: Weeks 4–6 (October 5 – October 16, 2026). Deliverables: Gap analysis report, benchmark comparison, compliance assessment. Phase 3 – Design & Recommendations: Weeks 7–10 (October 19 – November 13, 2026). Deliverables: Optimized workflow designs, technology recommendations, implementation roadmap. Phase 4 – Validation & Handoff: Weeks 11–12 (November 16 – November 27, 2026). Deliverables: Executive presentation, knowledge transfer sessions, final documentation package. Project completion target: November 27, 2026. All timelines assume weekly engagement cadence and timely availability of FIRMA stakeholders for interviews and review sessions.
sections.pricing: [TO BE CONFIRMED] – The proposed engagement budget is USD 12,000 for the three-month period. This covers Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect time for discovery, analysis, design, and knowledge transfer activities. Detailed rate breakdown, payment schedule (e.g., monthly installments or milestone-based), and any additional resource allocation (e.g., junior analyst support, specialized technical expertise) will be finalized during contract negotiation based on confirmed scope and resource requirements.
sections.next_steps: 1. Contract Execution – Koya Talent will prepare a Statement of Work (SOW) detailing the engagement terms, deliverables, timeline, and pricing. FIRMA and Koya Talent will execute the SOW by [TO BE CONFIRMED]. 2. Kickoff Meeting – Upon contract execution, we will schedule a formal kickoff meeting with Adejumo, Sarah Chen, and key FIRMA stakeholders (HR, Finance, Payroll, IT leads) to align on objectives, confirm access to systems and personnel, and establish communication protocols. 3. Stakeholder Engagement – FIRMA will designate a primary point of contact and ensure availability of relevant team members for interviews and review sessions throughout the engagement. 4. System & Documentation Access – FIRMA will provide Koya Talent with read-only access to relevant payroll systems, banking integration documentation, and process documentation to support discovery activities. 5. Weekly Status Cadence – Koya Talent and FIRMA will establish a weekly 30-minute status call to track progress, address blockers, and confirm upcoming deliverable reviews. For questions or to proceed, please contact Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) or reply directly to this proposal. We look forward to partnering with FIRMA to optimize your employee salary payment processes.

sections.introduction: Nit Tech currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating operational friction and delaying critical financial close cycles. This proposal outlines a comprehensive automation initiative designed to eliminate manual touchpoints, accelerate invoice processing through intelligent OCR reconciliation, and provide real-time executive visibility via a purpose-built KPI dashboard. Koya Talent will deliver a fully integrated, SOC 2 Type II compliant solution leveraging Supabase architecture and REST API integration with your existing ERP system. The engagement spans 8 weeks across three structured delivery phases, culminating in a production-ready platform that reclaims 25+ hours of weekly operational capacity and strengthens financial governance.
sections.project_scope: This engagement addresses three interconnected operational bottlenecks: (1) Manual Carrier Onboarding – currently requiring duplicate data entry, email-based coordination, and ad-hoc spreadsheet management; (2) Invoice Reconciliation Delays – invoices are manually matched against purchase orders and receipts, creating reconciliation backlogs and payment delays; (3) Executive Visibility Gap – leadership lacks real-time insight into carrier performance, invoice aging, and reconciliation status. The solution scope encompasses: automated carrier onboarding workflow with role-based approval gates; intelligent invoice OCR engine capable of extracting line-item detail and matching against ERP records; executive KPI dashboard surfacing carrier onboarding velocity, invoice aging, reconciliation accuracy, and payment cycle metrics. Integration points include REST API connectivity to your existing ERP system for real-time data synchronization, SOC 2 Type II compliance architecture ensuring data security and audit readiness, and Supabase-backed infrastructure providing scalable, secure data persistence. Out-of-scope: custom ERP modifications, third-party carrier system integrations beyond REST API, and post-launch 24/7 managed services (support model to be defined separately).
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will employ a phased, agile delivery methodology grounded in recruitment operations consulting best practices and modern cloud architecture. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) focuses on Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design: detailed process mapping of current carrier onboarding and invoice workflows, ERP API specification review, Supabase schema design for carrier profiles, invoice records, and reconciliation state, and SOC 2 Type II compliance framework documentation. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6) executes Core Platform Development: Supabase backend provisioning with role-based access control (RBAC), RESTful API layer for ERP integration, carrier onboarding workflow engine with approval routing, invoice OCR module leveraging industry-standard document processing, and executive KPI dashboard frontend. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8) covers Integration Testing, UAT, and Production Deployment: end-to-end testing of carrier onboarding workflows, invoice reconciliation accuracy validation against sample datasets, ERP API integration verification, SOC 2 Type II compliance audit preparation, and production cutover with rollback contingency. Throughout the engagement, Koya Talent will assign a dedicated Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect as engagement lead, supported by a Supabase specialist and recruitment operations consultant. Weekly stakeholder syncs will track progress against milestones, surface blockers, and validate alignment with Nit Tech's operational priorities.
sections.deliverables: 1. Requirements & Architecture Documentation (Week 2): Detailed process flow diagrams for carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation; ERP API integration specification; Supabase data model and schema design; SOC 2 Type II compliance roadmap and security controls matrix. 2. Carrier Onboarding Platform (Week 5): Fully functional Supabase-backed carrier profile management system; automated workflow engine with multi-stage approval gates (e.g., compliance review, finance approval); role-based access control for operations, finance, and executive users; audit logging for all onboarding state transitions. 3. Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine (Week 6): Document ingestion pipeline accepting PDF and image uploads; OCR extraction module returning structured line-item data (vendor, amount, date, PO reference); automated matching logic against ERP purchase orders and receipts; reconciliation dashboard surfacing matched, unmatched, and exception invoices. 4. Executive KPI Dashboard (Week 6): Real-time metrics including carrier onboarding velocity (new carriers per week), invoice aging (days outstanding by vendor), reconciliation accuracy (% matched invoices), and payment cycle efficiency; drill-down capability to underlying transaction detail; role-based view filtering (e.g., finance sees all metrics; operations sees carrier-specific KPIs). 5. ERP Integration Layer (Week 6): RESTful API client for bidirectional data sync with your existing ERP; automated carrier master data synchronization; purchase order and receipt data retrieval for reconciliation matching; payment status updates flowing back to ERP. 6. SOC 2 Type II Compliance Package (Week 8): Security controls documentation; data encryption specifications (in-transit and at-rest); access control policies and audit logging configuration; compliance readiness report and remediation checklist. 7. Deployment & Handover Documentation (Week 8): Production deployment runbook; system administration guide; end-user training materials for operations and finance teams; post-launch support escalation procedures.
sections.timeline: Phase 1 – Requirements & Architecture (Weeks 1–2): Week 1 includes discovery call debrief, stakeholder interviews, and ERP API documentation review. Week 2 delivers architecture design review, Supabase schema finalization, and compliance framework sign-off. Phase 2 – Core Development (Weeks 3–6): Week 3 begins Supabase environment provisioning and backend API scaffolding. Weeks 4–5 focus on carrier onboarding workflow implementation and invoice OCR module development. Week 6 completes ERP integration, KPI dashboard frontend, and initial integration testing. Phase 3 – Testing & Deployment (Weeks 7–8): Week 7 executes end-to-end UAT with Nit Tech operations and finance teams, invoice reconciliation accuracy validation, and SOC 2 compliance audit. Week 8 finalizes production deployment, cutover execution, and team handover training. Critical milestones: Architecture sign-off (end of Week 2); Carrier onboarding workflow MVP ready for internal testing (end of Week 4); Invoice OCR accuracy threshold validated (end of Week 5); Full platform UAT completion (end of Week 7); Production go-live (end of Week 8). Testing windows: Continuous integration testing throughout Weeks 3–6; dedicated UAT environment available to Nit Tech stakeholders during Week 7; production deployment window scheduled for end of Week 8 with rollback contingency.
sections.pricing: $48,000 fixed milestone fee, structured as follows: 40% ($19,200) due upon engagement commencement and architecture sign-off (end of Week 2); 35% ($16,800) due upon completion of core platform development and integration testing (end of Week 6); 25% ($12,000) due upon production deployment and handover completion (end of Week 8). This fixed-fee structure covers all labor, Supabase infrastructure provisioning, and deliverables outlined above. Excluded from this fee: post-launch managed services, ongoing support retainers, third-party OCR licensing (if client opts for premium tier beyond baseline), and ERP system modifications. Travel and expenses: [TO BE CONFIRMED] based on engagement location and any on-site requirements. Optional add-ons available post-launch: 3-month managed support retainer, advanced OCR model tuning, and custom reporting module development.
sections.next_steps: 1. Proposal Review & Approval: Nit Tech leadership reviews this proposal and confirms alignment with business objectives and budget. 2. Engagement Agreement: Koya Talent will provide a Master Services Agreement (MSA) and Statement of Work (SOW) for signature by authorized Nit Tech representatives. 3. Kickoff Scheduling: Upon MSA execution, Koya Talent will schedule a formal project kickoff meeting with Nit Tech stakeholders (operations, finance, IT, and executive sponsor) to confirm requirements, introduce the delivery team, and establish communication cadence. 4. Access & Environment Setup: Nit Tech IT will provision Koya Talent team members with ERP API credentials, Supabase project access, and any required network/VPN connectivity. 5. Engagement Commencement: Week 1 activities begin immediately following access provisioning. Primary contact for this engagement is Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) and the assigned Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect. For technical questions, escalate to the Supabase specialist. For operational process questions, escalate to the recruitment operations consultant. All inquiries and change requests should be logged via the project management system (to be established during kickoff). Approval authority for scope changes and timeline adjustments resides with the Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect and Nit Tech's designated project sponsor. Questions or clarifications on this proposal should be directed to Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@koyatalent.com) or the engagement lead (contact details to be provided upon MSA execution).

intake_data.client_needs_summary: Manual carrier onboarding and delayed invoice reconciliation causing 25 hours/week of overhead.
intake_data.project_scope: Automated carrier onboarding workflow, invoice OCR reconciliation, and an executive KPI dashboard.
intake_data.target_roles: Recruitment Ops Consulting, Workflow Automation, Supabase Architecture
intake_data.constraints: Must integrate with existing ERP via REST APIs. SOC 2 Type II compliance required.

sections.introduction: Acme Logistics currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating operational bottlenecks and limiting scalability. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design and implement an automated carrier onboarding workflow, invoice OCR-driven reconciliation system, and executive KPI dashboard. The solution will integrate seamlessly with Acme's existing ERP infrastructure via REST APIs while maintaining SOC 2 Type II compliance. By automating these critical processes, Acme will recover significant operational capacity, reduce reconciliation errors, and gain real-time visibility into carrier performance and financial metrics.
sections.project_scope: This engagement encompasses three core workstreams: (1) Carrier Onboarding Automation – design and build a workflow that eliminates manual data entry, validates carrier credentials against regulatory databases, and routes approvals through defined governance gates; (2) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation – implement intelligent document processing to extract invoice line items, match them against purchase orders and receipts, flag discrepancies, and auto-post to the ERP; and (3) Executive KPI Dashboard – develop a real-time analytics interface surfacing carrier performance metrics, invoice aging, reconciliation status, and cost trends. The solution must integrate with Acme's existing ERP via REST APIs and achieve SOC 2 Type II certification. Out of scope: migration of historical invoice data (data cleansing and bulk import will be scoped separately if required), custom ERP modifications beyond API integration, and third-party carrier database licensing.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will employ a phased, agile delivery model leveraging Supabase as the core application platform, combined with Recruitment Ops consulting expertise to optimize workflow design. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) focuses on discovery, API audit, and workflow design workshops with Acme stakeholders to map current-state processes and define automation rules. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6) delivers the carrier onboarding module, invoice OCR integration (via third-party OCR provider), and reconciliation engine, with iterative testing and ERP API integration. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8) completes the KPI dashboard, conducts end-to-end testing, prepares SOC 2 Type II compliance documentation, and executes knowledge transfer. The architecture will employ Supabase PostgreSQL for transactional data, serverless functions for workflow orchestration, and REST API connectors to Acme's ERP. All code will follow security best practices, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control, and audit logging to support compliance certification.
sections.deliverables: 1. Workflow Design Documentation – detailed process maps, approval matrices, and automation rules for carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation. 2. Carrier Onboarding Module – fully functional web application with form validation, credential verification, document upload, and approval workflow. 3. Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – OCR integration, line-item extraction, PO matching logic, discrepancy flagging, and ERP posting automation. 4. Executive KPI Dashboard – real-time analytics interface with carrier performance, invoice aging, reconciliation metrics, and cost trend visualizations. 5. ERP API Integration Layer – REST API connectors, data transformation logic, and error handling for bidirectional ERP synchronization. 6. SOC 2 Type II Compliance Package – security audit report, access control documentation, encryption specifications, and audit log configuration. 7. Knowledge Transfer & Training – recorded walkthroughs, runbooks, and live training session for Acme operations and IT teams. 8. Source Code Repository – fully documented, version-controlled codebase with deployment scripts and environment configuration templates.
sections.timeline: Phase 1 – Discovery & Design (Weeks 1–2): Stakeholder interviews, ERP API audit, workflow mapping workshops, and technical architecture review. Deliverable: Workflow design document and API integration plan. Phase 2 – Build & Integration (Weeks 3–6): Carrier onboarding module development, OCR integration, reconciliation engine build, ERP API connector development, and iterative testing. Deliverables: Functional modules, API integration, and test results. Phase 3 – Dashboard, Compliance & Launch (Weeks 7–8): KPI dashboard development, SOC 2 Type II compliance documentation, end-to-end testing, knowledge transfer sessions, and production deployment. Deliverables: Live dashboard, compliance package, training materials, and source code handoff. Go-live target: End of Week 8. Post-launch support window: [TO BE CONFIRMED].
sections.pricing: Fixed Milestone Fee: $48,000 across three phases. Breakdown: Phase 1 (Discovery & Design) – $12,000; Phase 2 (Build & Integration) – $24,000; Phase 3 (Dashboard, Compliance & Launch) – $12,000. Payment schedule: 50% upon engagement signature, 25% upon Phase 2 completion, 25% upon go-live. Out-of-scope work (e.g., historical data migration, custom ERP modifications, extended post-launch support beyond knowledge transfer) will be quoted separately on a time-and-materials basis at [TO BE CONFIRMED] per hour. Third-party OCR service costs (if not already licensed by Acme) are excluded and should be budgeted separately.
sections.next_steps: 1. Proposal Review & Approval – Rachel Adams and Sarah Chen to review this proposal and confirm alignment with Acme's objectives and timeline. 2. Engagement Agreement – Koya Talent will provide a Master Services Agreement and Statement of Work for signature by both parties. 3. Kickoff Meeting – Upon signature, schedule a 90-minute kickoff call with Acme stakeholders (Rachel Adams, IT lead, operations lead) and Koya Talent delivery team to confirm scope, establish communication cadence, and initiate Phase 1 discovery. 4. Access & Environment Setup – Acme to provide sandbox ERP credentials, API documentation, and Supabase project access for Koya Talent development team. 5. Weekly Standups – Bi-weekly progress reviews and weekly async updates via Slack/email. Primary contact: Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@koyatalent.com). For technical questions, Koya Talent will assign a Principal Architect as the technical lead. Target engagement start date: [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Please confirm acceptance and proposed start date by [TO BE CONFIRMED].

proposals.supporting_material:
CLIENT ARCHITECTURAL CRITERIA & BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS:
- Organization: Astra Global Financial Services
- Primary Executive Contact: Excellence Jumo (Chief Technology Officer)
- Current Infrastructure: On-premise monolithic architecture encountering throughput bottlenecks during peak trading hours.
- Target State: Resilient multi-region cloud deployment on Google Cloud & AWS, containerized microservices managed by Kubernetes, and automated KYC pipelines processing under 3 seconds per verification.
- Compliance Mandates: Strict adherence to SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 specifications.
- Commercial Framework: $145,000 total investment phased over three milestone gates: Phase 1 ($45,000), Phase 2 ($60,000), Phase 3 ($40,000).
- Delivery Horizon: 12 weeks from contract execution with bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews.

sections.introduction: Astra Global Financial Services is undertaking a strategic transformation to migrate from a legacy on-premise monolithic architecture to a resilient, multi-region cloud infrastructure capable of supporting high-throughput transaction processing with 99.99% availability. This engagement will deliver an end-to-end cloud modernization program coupled with an automated Know Your Customer (KYC) verification platform, real-time Anti-Money Laundering (AML) surveillance capabilities, and comprehensive regulatory compliance across SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 standards. Koya Talent will provide dedicated enterprise solutions architecture, DevOps engineering, and financial systems compliance expertise to architect, implement, and operationalize this transformation over a 12-week phased delivery cycle. The engagement is structured around three milestone gates with executive steering committee governance, ensuring alignment with Astra's business objectives and regulatory obligations.
sections.project_scope: This engagement encompasses the complete modernization of Astra Global Financial Services' technology infrastructure and identity verification operations. The scope includes: (1) Assessment and design of multi-region cloud architecture spanning Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services with containerized microservices orchestrated via Kubernetes; (2) Migration of monolithic on-premise systems to cloud-native, horizontally scalable services addressing current peak-hour throughput bottlenecks; (3) Design and implementation of automated KYC verification microservices capable of processing identity verifications in under 3 seconds per transaction; (4) Encrypted event stream infrastructure for secure, auditable transaction flows; (5) Real-time AML surveillance dashboard providing operational visibility into transaction patterns and compliance risk indicators; (6) Comprehensive security hardening aligned with PCI-DSS Level 1, SOC2 Type II, and ISO 27001 requirements; (7) Establishment of CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code frameworks, and automated compliance monitoring; (8) Knowledge transfer and operational runbook documentation for Astra's internal teams. The engagement explicitly excludes legacy system decommissioning, third-party vendor integrations beyond scope definition, and post-go-live production support beyond the 12-week delivery window. All deliverables will be validated against the 99.99% availability SLA and regulatory compliance mandates prior to production handoff.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, risk-mitigated delivery model structured around three milestone gates with continuous executive governance. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) focuses on discovery, architectural design, and pilot environment establishment. Our Lead Cloud Solutions Architect will conduct detailed current-state assessment of on-premise infrastructure, document technical debt and throughput constraints, and design the target multi-cloud architecture incorporating Google Cloud and AWS services. We will establish a pilot Kubernetes cluster in a non-production environment and prototype the KYC microservices framework to validate sub-3-second verification latency assumptions. Phase 2 (Weeks 5–9) centers on core infrastructure migration and microservices development. The Senior DevOps Engineer will implement production-grade multi-region cloud infrastructure with automated failover, configure encrypted event streams using managed services (e.g., Google Pub/Sub, AWS Kinesis), and deploy containerized KYC verification services. The Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will embed compliance controls into infrastructure-as-code templates, establish audit logging, and validate PCI-DSS and SOC2 control implementations. Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12) encompasses AML dashboard deployment, end-to-end testing, compliance validation, and production cutover. A 2-week pilot verification window will run parallel production validation before final go-live. Throughout delivery, bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews will track milestone completion, risk mitigation, and budget adherence. All infrastructure will be defined as code, version-controlled, and subject to automated compliance scanning. The approach prioritizes operational resilience, regulatory defensibility, and knowledge transfer to Astra's internal teams.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs across the 12-week engagement: (1) Multi-Cloud Architecture Design Document – comprehensive technical specification for Google Cloud and AWS infrastructure, including network topology, security zones, disaster recovery strategy, and 99.99% availability design patterns; (2) Kubernetes Cluster Configuration & Deployment Manifests – production-ready cluster definitions, auto-scaling policies, and container orchestration templates for both cloud regions; (3) KYC Verification Microservices Codebase – containerized, API-driven identity verification services with sub-3-second latency validation, comprehensive logging, and error handling; (4) Encrypted Event Stream Infrastructure – managed event broker configuration (Pub/Sub/Kinesis), schema definitions, encryption key management, and audit trail logging; (5) Real-Time AML Surveillance Dashboard – operational UI providing transaction monitoring, risk scoring, alert management, and compliance reporting capabilities; (6) Infrastructure-as-Code Repository – Terraform/CloudFormation templates for repeatable, auditable infrastructure provisioning across environments; (7) PCI-DSS & SOC2 Compliance Validation Report – detailed control mapping, evidence artifacts, and remediation documentation; (8) CI/CD Pipeline Configuration – automated build, test, and deployment workflows with security scanning and compliance gates; (9) Operational Runbooks & Knowledge Transfer Documentation – step-by-step procedures for infrastructure management, incident response, and KYC service operations; (10) Pilot Verification Test Plan & Results – documented validation of 99.99% availability SLA, KYC latency targets, and regulatory compliance during 2-week parallel production window. Deliverables will be version-controlled in a shared repository, reviewed at each milestone gate, and formally handed off to Astra's operations team. Koya Talent will assign: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (full engagement), Senior DevOps Engineer (full engagement), and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (Weeks 1–4 and 9–12 intensive, with advisory availability in Weeks 5–8).
sections.timeline: The engagement follows a 12-week phased delivery schedule with three milestone gates and bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews. Phase 1: Discovery & Pilot Environment (Weeks 1–4, Milestone Gate 1 at end of Week 4) – Current-state infrastructure assessment, target architecture design, pilot Kubernetes cluster provisioning, KYC microservices prototype development, and compliance requirements mapping. Deliverables: Architecture Design Document, Pilot Environment, KYC Prototype. Phase 2: Core Infrastructure & Microservices Migration (Weeks 5–9, Milestone Gate 2 at end of Week 9) – Multi-region cloud infrastructure deployment, containerized service migration, encrypted event stream implementation, compliance control embedding, and infrastructure-as-code repository establishment. Deliverables: Production Cloud Infrastructure, Microservices Codebase, Event Stream Configuration, Compliance Validation Report (draft). Phase 3: AML Dashboard, Testing & Go-Live (Weeks 10–12, Milestone Gate 3 at end of Week 12) – AML surveillance dashboard deployment, end-to-end integration testing, 2-week pilot verification window (overlapping Weeks 11–12), final compliance validation, operational runbook completion, and production cutover. Deliverables: AML Dashboard, Pilot Verification Results, Final Compliance Report, Operational Runbooks, Knowledge Transfer Completion. Executive steering committee reviews occur bi-weekly (Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12) to track milestone progress, risk mitigation, budget adherence, and stakeholder alignment. All testing windows, including the 2-week pilot verification, are scheduled within the 12-week window to validate 99.99% availability SLA and regulatory compliance prior to production handoff.
sections.pricing: Koya Talent's engagement is structured as a fixed-fee delivery model totaling $145,000 USD, phased across three milestone gates aligned with project deliverables and risk reduction. Milestone 1 (Weeks 1–4, Discovery & Pilot): $45,000 – Due upon completion of Phase 1 deliverables (Architecture Design Document, Pilot Environment, KYC Prototype, Compliance Requirements Mapping). Milestone 2 (Weeks 5–9, Core Infrastructure & Migration): $60,000 – Due upon completion of Phase 2 deliverables (Production Cloud Infrastructure, Microservices Codebase, Event Stream Configuration, Draft Compliance Validation Report). Milestone 3 (Weeks 10–12, AML Dashboard & Go-Live): $40,000 – Due upon completion of Phase 3 deliverables (AML Dashboard, Pilot Verification Results, Final Compliance Report, Operational Runbooks, Knowledge Transfer). The fixed fee covers all labor for the assigned team (Lead Cloud Solutions Architect, Senior DevOps Engineer, Financial Systems Compliance Specialist), technical design, implementation, testing, and knowledge transfer. The fee does not include: cloud infrastructure consumption costs (Google Cloud and AWS usage charges are Astra's responsibility), third-party software licenses beyond open-source frameworks, or post-go-live production support beyond the 12-week delivery window. Payment terms are Net 30 from invoice date. Invoices will be issued upon milestone completion and formal acceptance by Astra's project sponsor. Any scope expansion, extended timeline, or additional resource allocation beyond the defined engagement will be subject to change order and separate commercial negotiation.
sections.next_steps: To proceed with this engagement, the following actions are required: (1) Formal Engagement Agreement – Astra Global Financial Services and Koya Talent will execute a Statement of Work (SOW) incorporating this proposal, defining roles, responsibilities, escalation procedures, and acceptance criteria for each milestone. The SOW will reference this proposal as the technical specification baseline. (2) Kickoff Meeting – Within 5 business days of SOW execution, Koya Talent's Lead Cloud Solutions Architect, Senior DevOps Engineer, and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will conduct a formal project kickoff with Astra's CTO (Excellence Jumo), project sponsor, and key technical stakeholders to confirm scope, establish communication protocols, and schedule bi-weekly steering committee reviews. (3) Access & Environment Provisioning – Astra will provide Koya Talent team members with necessary access to current on-premise infrastructure, cloud platform accounts (Google Cloud and AWS), version control repositories, and compliance documentation required for Phase 1 discovery. (4) Governance & Steering Committee – Astra will designate a project sponsor and confirm bi-weekly steering committee meeting schedule (recommended: Tuesdays, 10:00 AM UTC). (5) Contract Execution – Both parties will sign the SOW and this proposal by [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Engagement commencement is targeted for [TO BE CONFIRMED], with Phase 1 kickoff occurring within 5 business days of contract execution. For questions, clarifications, or to schedule the kickoff meeting, please contact Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) at [TO BE CONFIRMED] or Excellence Jumo at excellencejumo@outlook.com. Koya Talent is committed to delivering a transformational cloud modernization and compliance-ready KYC platform that positions Astra Global Financial Services for scalable, resilient growth.

proposals.supporting_material:
CLIENT ARCHITECTURAL CRITERIA & BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS:
- Organization: Astra Global Financial Services
- Primary Executive Contact: Excellence Jumo (Chief Technology Officer)
- Current Infrastructure: On-premise monolithic architecture encountering throughput bottlenecks during peak trading hours.
- Target State: Resilient multi-region cloud deployment on Google Cloud & AWS, containerized microservices managed by Kubernetes, and automated KYC pipelines processing under 3 seconds per verification.
- Compliance Mandates: Strict adherence to SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 specifications.
- Commercial Framework: $145,000 total investment phased over three milestone gates: Phase 1 ($45,000), Phase 2 ($60,000), Phase 3 ($40,000).
- Delivery Horizon: 12 weeks from contract execution with bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews.

sections.introduction: Astra Global Financial Services is undertaking a strategic transformation to modernize its financial infrastructure and enhance regulatory compliance posture. Currently, the organization operates a monolithic on-premise architecture that experiences throughput bottlenecks during peak trading hours, limiting transaction velocity and operational resilience. This proposal outlines Koya Talent's comprehensive engagement to architect and deliver a resilient multi-region cloud deployment spanning Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services, implement automated identity verification microservices capable of sub-3-second KYC processing, and establish real-time AML surveillance capabilities—all while maintaining strict adherence to SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance frameworks. The 12-week phased delivery model ensures controlled risk mitigation, continuous stakeholder alignment, and measurable business value realization at each milestone gate.
sections.project_scope: Astra Global Financial Services requires end-to-end modernization spanning infrastructure, application architecture, and compliance governance. The current on-premise monolithic system exhibits critical performance constraints during peak trading periods, necessitating immediate architectural intervention. The engagement encompasses: (1) Multi-cloud infrastructure migration across Google Cloud Platform and AWS with automated failover and multi-region redundancy to achieve 99.99% availability SLA; (2) Decomposition of legacy monolithic systems into containerized microservices orchestrated by Kubernetes, enabling independent scaling and deployment velocity; (3) Automated KYC verification pipeline redesign to process identity verification requests in under 3 seconds per transaction, replacing manual or batch-oriented workflows; (4) Encrypted event streaming architecture for asynchronous transaction processing and audit trail immutability; (5) Real-time AML surveillance dashboard providing continuous transaction monitoring, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting; (6) Full SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance implementation including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, audit logging, and incident response procedures. Key constraints include adherence to enterprise security guidelines, zero-downtime migration requirements for production trading systems, and regulatory approval timelines. Success metrics include sub-3-second KYC processing latency, 99.99% platform availability, zero compliance audit findings, and measurable reduction in peak-hour transaction processing delays.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, risk-mitigated cloud modernization strategy grounded in industry best practices for financial services transformation. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) focuses on discovery, architecture design, and pilot infrastructure provisioning. Our Lead Cloud Solutions Architect will conduct detailed technical assessments of the current monolithic system, map data flows, identify compliance gaps, and design the target multi-cloud architecture. We will establish a pilot Google Cloud Platform environment with Kubernetes cluster provisioning, implement foundational identity and access management (IAM) policies aligned with PCI-DSS, and deploy initial KYC microservice prototypes. A 2-week pilot verification window will validate performance assumptions, security controls, and regulatory compliance posture before full-scale rollout. Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) executes production infrastructure deployment and microservices migration. The Senior DevOps Engineer will provision multi-region AWS and GCP infrastructure with automated failover, implement encrypted event streaming (Apache Kafka or Google Pub/Sub), containerize legacy KYC and AML components, and establish CI/CD pipelines for continuous deployment. The Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will implement SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 controls, configure encryption key management, establish audit logging, and conduct preliminary compliance testing. Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) focuses on production cutover, real-time AML dashboard deployment, and compliance certification. We will execute controlled traffic migration from on-premise to cloud infrastructure, deploy the real-time AML surveillance dashboard with anomaly detection algorithms, conduct full SOC2 and PCI-DSS compliance audits, and establish operational runbooks and incident response procedures. Bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews will ensure stakeholder alignment and enable rapid decision-making on critical path items. This approach minimizes production risk through staged validation, maintains regulatory compliance throughout the transition, and delivers measurable business value at each milestone.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete, measurable outputs across three milestone gates: PHASE 1 DELIVERABLES (Week 4): (1) Comprehensive current-state technical assessment documenting monolithic architecture, performance bottlenecks, and compliance gaps; (2) Target-state multi-cloud architecture design document specifying Google Cloud Platform and AWS infrastructure topology, Kubernetes cluster design, and disaster recovery procedures; (3) Pilot Kubernetes cluster on Google Cloud Platform with foundational IAM policies, network segmentation, and PCI-DSS baseline controls; (4) Prototype KYC microservice (containerized, API-driven) demonstrating sub-3-second processing latency; (5) 2-week pilot verification report validating performance, security, and compliance assumptions; (6) Detailed Phase 2 and Phase 3 execution roadmap with resource allocation and risk mitigation strategies. PHASE 2 DELIVERABLES (Week 8): (1) Production-grade multi-region infrastructure on AWS and GCP with automated failover, load balancing, and 99.99% availability architecture; (2) Encrypted event streaming platform (Kafka or Pub/Sub) with audit trail immutability and compliance-grade retention policies; (3) Containerized microservices for KYC verification, AML transaction screening, and identity management deployed to production Kubernetes clusters; (4) CI/CD pipeline infrastructure enabling automated testing, security scanning, and continuous deployment; (5) SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 control implementation including encryption key management, role-based access controls, and audit logging; (6) Preliminary compliance testing report documenting control effectiveness and remediation status. PHASE 3 DELIVERABLES (Week 12): (1) Real-time AML surveillance dashboard with transaction monitoring, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting capabilities; (2) Production traffic migration completion with zero-downtime cutover validation; (3) Final SOC2 Type II and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance certification with auditor sign-off; (4) Operational runbooks, incident response procedures, and on-call escalation protocols; (5) Knowledge transfer sessions and documentation enabling Astra Global's internal teams to operate and maintain the platform independently; (6) Post-implementation review documenting lessons learned, performance metrics, and recommendations for future enhancements. RESOURCE ALLOCATION: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (full-time, Weeks 1–12) responsible for architecture design, multi-cloud strategy, and compliance framework alignment; Senior DevOps Engineer (full-time, Weeks 1–12) responsible for infrastructure provisioning, containerization, CI/CD pipeline implementation, and production operations; Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (full-time, Weeks 1–12) responsible for SOC2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliance implementation, audit coordination, and regulatory documentation.
sections.timeline: The 12-week engagement is structured as three phased delivery milestones with integrated testing, compliance validation, and stakeholder governance: PHASE 1: DISCOVERY, DESIGN & PILOT VERIFICATION (Weeks 1–4, Milestone Gate 1 – $45,000): Week 1–2: Current-state technical assessment, stakeholder interviews, compliance gap analysis, and target architecture design workshops. Week 2–3: Pilot Kubernetes cluster provisioning on Google Cloud Platform, IAM policy implementation, and foundational security controls deployment. Week 3–4: KYC microservice prototype development and deployment to pilot environment. Week 4: 2-week pilot verification window begins (concurrent with Phase 2 planning). Milestone Gate 1 Review: Executive steering committee sign-off on architecture design, pilot results, and Phase 2 execution plan. PHASE 2: PRODUCTION INFRASTRUCTURE & MICROSERVICES MIGRATION (Weeks 5–8, Milestone Gate 2 – $60,000): Week 5–6: Multi-region AWS and GCP infrastructure provisioning, network segmentation, and disaster recovery configuration. Week 6–7: Encrypted event streaming platform deployment, containerized microservices migration, and CI/CD pipeline implementation. Week 7–8: SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 control implementation, encryption key management, and preliminary compliance testing. Milestone Gate 2 Review: Executive steering committee validation of infrastructure readiness, compliance control effectiveness, and Phase 3 cutover plan. PHASE 3: PRODUCTION CUTOVER & COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATION (Weeks 9–12, Milestone Gate 3 – $40,000): Week 9–10: Real-time AML surveillance dashboard development and deployment. Week 10–11: Controlled production traffic migration with zero-downtime cutover validation. Week 11–12: Final SOC2 Type II and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance audits, operational runbook finalization, and knowledge transfer sessions. Milestone Gate 3 Review: Executive steering committee sign-off on production readiness, compliance certification, and operational handoff. GOVERNANCE: Bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews (Tuesdays, 10:00 AM UTC) with attendance from Astra Global CTO Excellence Jumo, Koya Talent engagement leadership, and key stakeholder representatives. Weekly technical working group meetings (Thursdays, 2:00 PM UTC) for detailed progress tracking, issue resolution, and risk mitigation. All deliverables subject to formal acceptance criteria and sign-off before milestone payment release.
sections.pricing: Koya Talent's engagement is structured as a fixed-fee, milestone-based commercial model totaling $145,000 across three delivery phases: PHASE 1 MILESTONE (Weeks 1–4): $45,000 – Payable upon executive steering committee approval of current-state assessment, target architecture design, pilot verification results, and Phase 2 execution plan. PHASE 2 MILESTONE (Weeks 5–8): $60,000 – Payable upon executive steering committee approval of production infrastructure deployment, microservices migration completion, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 control implementation, and Phase 3 cutover readiness. PHASE 3 MILESTONE (Weeks 9–12): $40,000 – Payable upon executive steering committee approval of production cutover completion, real-time AML dashboard deployment, final SOC2 Type II and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance certification, and operational handoff. RESOURCE ALLOCATION: The engagement includes full-time allocation of three senior Koya Talent resources: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect, Senior DevOps Engineer, and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist across all 12 weeks. ASSUMPTIONS: Pricing assumes Astra Global provides timely access to current infrastructure, systems documentation, and key stakeholders for discovery and validation activities. Any scope expansion beyond the defined project scope (e.g., additional cloud regions, enhanced AML algorithms, extended compliance frameworks) will be subject to change order and separate commercial negotiation. Pricing excludes third-party cloud infrastructure costs (Google Cloud Platform and AWS consumption), which will be billed separately by the respective cloud providers based on actual usage. PAYMENT TERMS: Net 30 from invoice date. Invoices issued upon milestone completion and executive steering committee sign-off.
sections.next_steps: To formalize this engagement and commence the 12-week delivery cycle, the following actions are required: (1) PROPOSAL ACCEPTANCE: Astra Global Financial Services must formally accept this proposal and authorize commencement of Phase 1 activities. Acceptance should be communicated in writing to Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) and Excellence Jumo (CTO). (2) MASTER SERVICE AGREEMENT EXECUTION: Koya Talent and Astra Global will execute a Master Service Agreement (MSA) incorporating this proposal as a Statement of Work (SOW), defining liability limitations, confidentiality obligations, and dispute resolution procedures. Legal review and signature are anticipated within 5 business days. (3) RESOURCE ONBOARDING: Upon MSA execution, Koya Talent's Lead Cloud Solutions Architect, Senior DevOps Engineer, and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will be formally assigned to the engagement. Onboarding activities include security clearance verification, NDA execution, and access provisioning to Astra Global's current infrastructure and systems. (4) DISCOVERY KICKOFF: Week 1 commences with a formal project kickoff meeting (target: within 3 business days of MSA execution) attended by Astra Global's CTO, key technical stakeholders, and Koya Talent engagement leadership. Discovery activities, stakeholder interviews, and current-state assessment will begin immediately. (5) GOVERNANCE ESTABLISHMENT: Bi-weekly executive steering committee meetings and weekly technical working group meetings will be scheduled and calendar invitations distributed to all participants. (6) COMMUNICATION & ESCALATION: Primary contact for this engagement is Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative, sarah.chen@koyatalent.com). Technical escalations should be directed to the Lead Cloud Solutions Architect. Executive escalations should be directed to Koya Talent's Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect. All inquiries regarding proposal terms, timeline, or commercial structure should be directed to Sarah Chen. ANTICIPATED TIMELINE TO COMMENCEMENT: Assuming proposal acceptance and MSA execution within 5 business days, Phase 1 activities will commence within 10 business days of this proposal date. The 12-week delivery cycle will conclude with full production cutover and compliance certification by Week 12 from contract execution. We look forward to partnering with Astra Global Financial Services on this transformational engagement. Please confirm acceptance and authorize commencement at your earliest convenience.

Bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews will ensure stakeholder alignment and enable rapid decision-making on critical path items. PHASE 2 DELIVERABLES (Week 8): (1) Production-grade multi-region infrastructure on AWS and GCP with automated failover, load balancing, and 99.99% availability architecture; (2) Encrypted event streaming platform (Kafka or Pub/Sub) with audit trail immutability and compliance-grade retention policies; (3) Containerized microservices for KYC verification, AML transaction screening, and identity management deployed to production Kubernetes clusters; (4) CI/CD pipeline infrastructure enabling automated testing, security scanning, and continuous deployment; (5) SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 control implementation including encryption key management, role-based access controls, and audit logging; (6) Preliminary compliance testing report documenting control effectiveness and remediation status. PHASE 3 DELIVERABLES (Week 12): (1) Real-time AML surveillance dashboard with transaction monitoring, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting capabilities; (2) Production traffic migration completion with zero-downtime cutover validation; (3) Final SOC2 Type II and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance certification with auditor sign-off; (4) Operational runbooks, incident response procedures, and on-call escalation protocols; (5) Knowledge transfer sessions and documentation enabling Astra Global's internal teams to operate and maintain the platform independently; (6) Post-implementation review documenting lessons learned, performance metrics, and recommendations for future enhancements. sections_snapshot.timeline: The 12-week engagement is structured as three phased delivery milestones with integrated testing, compliance validation, and stakeholder governance: PHASE 1: DISCOVERY, DESIGN & PILOT VERIFICATION (Weeks 1–4, Milestone Gate 1 – $45,000): Week 1–2: Current-state technical assessment, stakeholder interviews, compliance gap analysis, and target architecture design workshops. Week 2–3: Pilot Kubernetes cluster provisioning on Google Cloud Platform, IAM policy implementation, and foundational security controls deployment. Week 3–4: KYC microservice prototype development and deployment to pilot environment. Week 4: 2-week pilot verification window begins (concurrent with Phase 2 planning). Milestone Gate 1 Review: Executive steering committee sign-off on architecture design, pilot results, and Phase 2 execution plan. PHASE 2: PRODUCTION INFRASTRUCTURE & MICROSERVICES MIGRATION (Weeks 5–8, Milestone Gate 2 – $60,000): Week 5–6: Multi-region AWS and GCP infrastructure provisioning, network segmentation, and disaster recovery configuration. sections.introduction: Koya Talent is pleased to present this proposal to Apex Enterprises 1789161781603 in response to the discovery conversation held on 2026-07-02 with Marcus Vance. Apex Enterprises has identified a critical business need: accelerating the delivery of qualified technical candidates to meet organizational growth and project timelines. This proposal outlines Koya Talent's structured approach to streamline candidate sourcing, vetting, and placement processes, enabling faster time-to-hire while maintaining rigorous quality standards aligned with enterprise hiring governance. Our engagement will focus on understanding Apex Enterprises' specific technical hiring requirements, candidate profile specifications, and organizational constraints to deliver a tailored talent acquisition solution.
sections.project_scope: The primary objective is to reduce candidate delivery timelines and improve hiring velocity for Apex Enterprises' technical roles. At this stage, the following elements require clarification and will be refined during the discovery and requirements-gathering phase: (1) Target technical roles and seniority levels (e.g., software engineers, cloud architects, data engineers, DevOps specialists); (2) Candidate volume requirements and hiring cadence (e.g., number of placements per quarter); (3) Specific technical competencies, certifications, and experience thresholds; (4) Geographic and remote work preferences; (5) Current hiring bottlenecks and pain points in the existing recruitment process; (6) Integration points with Apex Enterprises' existing talent management systems and HR workflows; (7) Compliance and security requirements within standard enterprise guidelines. Koya Talent will conduct a comprehensive discovery workshop with Marcus Vance and relevant stakeholders to map these requirements, establish baseline hiring metrics, and identify optimization opportunities. This scoping phase is essential to ensure the proposed solution directly addresses Apex Enterprises' unique constraints and business objectives.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will deploy a phased, data-driven talent acquisition acceleration model tailored to Apex Enterprises' enterprise environment. Phase 1 (Discovery & Requirements Refinement) will involve structured stakeholder interviews to document target roles, hiring volume, technical skill matrices, and current process inefficiencies. Phase 2 (Candidate Pipeline Development) will leverage Koya Talent's proprietary sourcing network, passive candidate engagement strategies, and technical screening frameworks to build a pre-qualified candidate pipeline aligned with Apex Enterprises' specifications. Phase 3 (Process Optimization & Integration) will establish streamlined workflows, define SLAs for candidate delivery, integrate with Apex Enterprises' applicant tracking system (ATS) and hiring tools, and implement quality assurance checkpoints. Phase 4 (Execution & Continuous Improvement) will execute placements, track key performance indicators (time-to-hire, candidate quality, offer acceptance rates), and conduct monthly performance reviews to refine sourcing and vetting strategies. Our methodology emphasizes transparency, regular communication, and measurable outcomes. We will provide weekly candidate pipeline reports, maintain a shared candidate tracking dashboard, and conduct bi-weekly business reviews to ensure alignment with Apex Enterprises' hiring objectives and organizational culture.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs and services: (1) Discovery & Requirements Documentation – A comprehensive technical hiring requirements matrix, candidate persona profiles, and process optimization roadmap; (2) Candidate Pipeline – Pre-qualified technical candidates matching Apex Enterprises' specifications, delivered on an agreed cadence (e.g., weekly or bi-weekly batches); (3) Screening & Assessment Reports – Detailed candidate profiles including technical competency assessments, reference checks, and cultural fit evaluations; (4) ATS Integration & Workflow Setup – Configuration of candidate tracking workflows, automated status updates, and reporting dashboards; (5) Hiring Process Documentation – Standard operating procedures (SOPs) for candidate intake, screening, interview coordination, and offer management; (6) Performance Analytics Dashboard – Real-time visibility into hiring metrics including time-to-hire, candidate source attribution, offer acceptance rates, and placement success rates; (7) Dedicated Account Management – A named Koya Talent Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect and supporting team will serve as primary contacts, ensuring continuity and strategic alignment throughout the engagement; (8) Monthly Business Reviews – Structured performance reviews with Marcus Vance and hiring stakeholders to assess progress, refine candidate profiles, and optimize delivery velocity. All deliverables will be documented in writing and tracked against agreed acceptance criteria.

Proposed timeframe: Within 10 business days of proposal acceptance. (2) Confirm Scope & Timeline – Based on discovery outputs, Koya Talent will deliver a detailed Statement of Work (SOW) with final timeline, deliverables, and pricing within 5 business days of the discovery workshop. (3) Execute Engagement Agreement – Upon SOW approval, Koya Talent and Apex Enterprises will execute a Master Service Agreement (MSA) and SOW, establishing legal terms, confidentiality obligations, and service level agreements. (4) Kick-Off & Onboarding – Koya Talent's dedicated account team will conduct a formal project kick-off, establish communication cadence, and begin Phase 1 activities. Primary Contact: Sarah Chen (Sales Representative) will facilitate initial coordination. For technical and delivery questions, contact the assigned Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect (to be confirmed upon engagement start). To proceed, please confirm Apex Enterprises' readiness to participate in the discovery workshop and authorize Marcus Vance as the primary stakeholder contact. We anticipate moving to contract execution within 15 business days of proposal acceptance, enabling candidate delivery to commence by [TO BE CONFIRMED].
