sections.introduction: Acme Logistics currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating operational friction and delayed financial close cycles. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design, build, and deploy an integrated automation platform comprising three core components: (1) an automated carrier onboarding workflow, (2) invoice OCR-driven reconciliation engine, and (3) an executive KPI dashboard for real-time visibility into logistics operations and financial metrics. The 8-week engagement will deliver measurable efficiency gains, reduced manual overhead, and improved data accuracy across carrier management and accounts payable functions.
sections.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational bottlenecks: (1) manual carrier onboarding requiring duplicate data entry, compliance verification, and document management across multiple systems, consuming an estimated 15 hours per week; and (2) invoice reconciliation requiring manual matching of carrier invoices to shipment records and PO data, consuming approximately 10 hours per week and introducing reconciliation delays of 5–10 business days. The proposed solution will automate end-to-end carrier onboarding via a self-service portal with integrated compliance checks, KYC validation, and document storage; deploy an OCR-powered invoice ingestion and matching engine to reconcile carrier invoices against shipment and contract data in near-real-time; and deliver an executive dashboard surfacing key performance indicators including carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice reconciliation accuracy, days sales outstanding (DSO), and carrier performance metrics. The engagement scope is bounded to Acme Logistics' primary carrier management and accounts payable workflows; integration with legacy ERP systems will follow standard enterprise API patterns; and deliverables will be hosted on cloud infrastructure aligned with Acme's existing security and compliance posture. Out-of-scope items include custom modifications to Acme's core ERP system, multi-tenant SaaS platform development, and ongoing managed services beyond the initial 8-week delivery window.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, agile delivery model structured across three 2–3 week sprints, with weekly stakeholder synchronization and iterative refinement based on user feedback. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) will focus on requirements discovery, technical architecture design, and integration planning, including detailed process mapping of current carrier onboarding and invoice workflows, identification of data sources and system integration points, and design of the OCR pipeline and dashboard data model. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6) will deliver the core platform components: (a) a carrier onboarding portal with role-based access control, document upload and validation, compliance checklist automation, and API-driven integration to Acme's carrier master data system; (b) an invoice OCR module leveraging industry-standard optical character recognition and machine learning to extract line-item data, match invoices to shipment records via fuzzy matching algorithms, and flag discrepancies for manual review; and (c) a preliminary executive dashboard with real-time KPI visualization, drill-down capability, and automated alert thresholds. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8) will encompass user acceptance testing (UAT), performance optimization, security hardening, knowledge transfer, and production deployment. The technical architecture will employ a microservices pattern with containerized deployment (Docker/Kubernetes), RESTful APIs for system integration, a cloud-hosted database (PostgreSQL or equivalent), and a modern frontend framework (React or Vue.js) for the user-facing portal and dashboard. All code will follow enterprise security standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control (RBAC), audit logging, and compliance with SOC 2 Type II controls.
sections.deliverables: The engagement will produce the following concrete, measurable deliverables: (1) Carrier Onboarding Portal – a fully functional, production-ready web application enabling carrier self-service registration, document upload, compliance verification, and real-time status tracking, with role-based access for Acme staff and carriers; (2) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – an automated pipeline ingesting carrier invoices (PDF, image, or email attachment), extracting structured line-item data via OCR, matching invoices to shipment and contract records with configurable matching rules, and generating exception reports for manual review; (3) Executive KPI Dashboard – a real-time analytics interface displaying carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice reconciliation accuracy (%), days to reconciliation, DSO, carrier performance scorecards, and historical trend analysis with drill-down and export capability; (4) API Integration Layer – RESTful APIs enabling bidirectional data sync between the onboarding portal, OCR engine, and Acme's existing ERP and carrier management systems; (5) Technical Documentation – comprehensive architecture diagrams, API specifications, deployment runbooks, and system administration guides; (6) User Training & Knowledge Transfer – live training sessions for Acme staff (estimated 4–6 hours), recorded video tutorials, and a detailed user manual covering portal navigation, invoice submission, dashboard interpretation, and troubleshooting; (7) Deployment & Infrastructure Setup – containerized application deployment to Acme's cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP per Acme's preference), database provisioning, SSL/TLS certificate configuration, and production readiness validation. All deliverables will be version-controlled, documented, and handed over with source code access and deployment automation (CI/CD pipelines) to enable Acme's internal teams to maintain and extend the platform post-engagement.
sections.timeline:
The engagement is structured as an accelerated 4-week fast track deployment, designed to deliver maximum value in minimal time while maintaining quality and stakeholder alignment.

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): Requirements Discovery, Architecture Design & Development Initiation**
Weeks 1–2 combine intensive discovery with parallel development preparation. Activities include detailed stakeholder interviews, process documentation, technical architecture design review, and integration point identification. The Architecture Design Review is completed by end of Week 1, enabling immediate development commencement. Simultaneously, the development team begins Sprint 1 work on the carrier onboarding portal foundation and OCR pipeline setup.

**Phase 2 (Weeks 2–3): Core Platform Development**
Development accelerates across two concurrent work streams. Sprint 1 (Weeks 2–3) delivers the carrier onboarding portal MVP with initial OCR capabilities and API integration layer. Sprint 2 (Weeks 2–3) delivers the invoice reconciliation engine and dashboard MVP. Daily standups replace weekly cadence to maintain momentum, with consolidated feedback sessions every Wednesday and Friday to ensure rapid iteration and stakeholder alignment.

**Phase 3 (Week 4): Testing, Optimization, Deployment & Knowledge Transfer**
Week 4 compresses final validation and go-live activities. User acceptance testing (UAT) with Acme stakeholders, performance optimization, security audit, and bug remediation occur in parallel during the first half of Week 4. Production deployment, post-deployment validation, and knowledge transfer completion occur in the second half of Week 4, with Production Go-Live targeted for end of Week 4.

**Critical Milestones:** Architecture Design Review (end of Week 1), Onboarding Portal MVP Demo (mid-Week 2), Full Platform Demo (end of Week 3), UAT Sign-Off (mid-Week 4), Production Go-Live (end of Week 4).

This accelerated timeline requires Acme to provide immediate and continuous access to stakeholders, system credentials, and data samples. Any delays in stakeholder availability or data access will proportionally impact the deployment schedule.
sections.pricing: Custom human-refined pricing structure: $54,000 across 3 strategic milestones with SLA guarantees.

Sarah Chen (Koya Talent Sales Representative) will coordinate contract execution and initial scheduling; the assigned Koya Talent Principal Enterprise Solutions Architect will serve as the primary delivery lead and single point of contact for all technical and project management matters. For questions or to confirm acceptance, please contact Sarah Chen or reply directly to this proposal. sections_snapshot.introduction: Acme Logistics currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating operational friction and delayed financial close cycles. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design, build, and deploy an integrated automation platform comprising three core components: (1) an automated carrier onboarding workflow, (2) invoice OCR-driven reconciliation engine, and (3) an executive KPI dashboard for real-time visibility into logistics operations and financial metrics. The 8-week engagement will deliver measurable efficiency gains, reduced manual overhead, and improved data accuracy across carrier management and accounts payable functions.
sections_snapshot.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational bottlenecks: (1) manual carrier onboarding requiring duplicate data entry, compliance verification, and document management across multiple systems, consuming an estimated 15 hours per week; and (2) invoice reconciliation requiring manual matching of carrier invoices to shipment records and PO data, consuming approximately 10 hours per week and introducing reconciliation delays of 5–10 business days. The proposed solution will automate end-to-end carrier onboarding via a self-service portal with integrated compliance checks, KYC validation, and document storage; deploy an OCR-powered invoice ingestion and matching engine to reconcile carrier invoices against shipment and contract data in near-real-time; and deliver an executive dashboard surfacing key performance indicators including carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice reconciliation accuracy, days sales outstanding (DSO), and carrier performance metrics. The engagement scope is bounded to Acme Logistics' primary carrier management and accounts payable workflows; integration with legacy ERP systems will follow standard enterprise API patterns; and deliverables will be hosted on cloud infrastructure aligned with Acme's existing security and compliance posture. Out-of-scope items include custom modifications to Acme's core ERP system, multi-tenant SaaS platform development, and ongoing managed services beyond the initial 8-week delivery window.
sections_snapshot.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, agile delivery model structured across three 2–3 week sprints, with weekly stakeholder synchronization and iterative refinement based on user feedback. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) will focus on requirements discovery, technical architecture design, and integration planning, including detailed process mapping of current carrier onboarding and invoice workflows, identification of data sources and system integration points, and design of the OCR pipeline and dashboard data model. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6) will deliver the core platform components: (a) a carrier onboarding portal with role-based access control, document upload and validation, compliance checklist automation, and API-driven integration to Acme's carrier master data system; (b) an invoice OCR module leveraging industry-standard optical character recognition and machine learning to extract line-item data, match invoices to shipment records via fuzzy matching algorithms, and flag discrepancies for manual review; and (c) a preliminary executive dashboard with real-time KPI visualization, drill-down capability, and automated alert thresholds. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8) will encompass user acceptance testing (UAT), performance optimization, security hardening, knowledge transfer, and production deployment. The technical architecture will employ a microservices pattern with containerized deployment (Docker/Kubernetes), RESTful APIs for system integration, a cloud-hosted database (PostgreSQL or equivalent), and a modern frontend framework (React or Vue.js) for the user-facing portal and dashboard. All code will follow enterprise security standards including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control (RBAC), audit logging, and compliance with SOC 2 Type II controls.
sections_snapshot.deliverables: The engagement will produce the following concrete, measurable deliverables: (1) Carrier Onboarding Portal – a fully functional, production-ready web application enabling carrier self-service registration, document upload, compliance verification, and real-time status tracking, with role-based access for Acme staff and carriers; (2) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – an automated pipeline ingesting carrier invoices (PDF, image, or email attachment), extracting structured line-item data via OCR, matching invoices to shipment and contract records with configurable matching rules, and generating exception reports for manual review; (3) Executive KPI Dashboard – a real-time analytics interface displaying carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice reconciliation accuracy (%), days to reconciliation, DSO, carrier performance scorecards, and historical trend analysis with drill-down and export capability; (4) API Integration Layer – RESTful APIs enabling bidirectional data sync between the onboarding portal, OCR engine, and Acme's existing ERP and carrier management systems; (5) Technical Documentation – comprehensive architecture diagrams, API specifications, deployment runbooks, and system administration guides; (6) User Training & Knowledge Transfer – live training sessions for Acme staff (estimated 4–6 hours), recorded video tutorials, and a detailed user manual covering portal navigation, invoice submission, dashboard interpretation, and troubleshooting; (7) Deployment & Infrastructure Setup – containerized application deployment to Acme's cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP per Acme's preference), database provisioning, SSL/TLS certificate configuration, and production readiness validation. All deliverables will be version-controlled, documented, and handed over with source code access and deployment automation (CI/CD pipelines) to enable Acme's internal teams to maintain and extend the platform post-engagement.

sections.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational pain points: (1) Manual Carrier Onboarding – new carrier registrations require duplicate data entry across multiple systems, manual document collection and verification, and ad-hoc communication workflows, consuming an estimated 12–15 hours per week and delaying carrier activation by 5–7 business days; (2) Invoice Reconciliation Delays – incoming carrier invoices are manually matched against shipment records, with discrepancies requiring escalation and rework, consuming an estimated 10–12 hours per week and creating a 3–5 day lag in payment processing and financial reporting. The project scope encompasses the following boundaries and deliverables: Automated Carrier Onboarding Workflow – design and implement a self-service carrier portal with guided data collection, document upload and validation, automated compliance checks (insurance, licensing, certifications), and real-time status notifications; Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – integrate optical character recognition (OCR) technology to extract invoice line items, automatically match invoices to shipment records using fuzzy matching and business rules, flag discrepancies and exceptions for manual review, and generate reconciliation reports; Executive KPI Dashboard – build a real-time analytics dashboard displaying carrier onboarding velocity, invoice reconciliation rates, payment aging, carrier performance scorecards, and operational efficiency trends. Out-of-scope items include: custom carrier billing system redesign, integration with third-party TMS platforms beyond standard APIs, multi-language support, or changes to existing financial accounting systems. The engagement assumes Acme Logistics maintains current versions of standard enterprise infrastructure (cloud hosting, relational databases, identity management) and operates under standard data security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, GDPR, or equivalent).
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will employ an agile, phased delivery methodology with three sequential sprints, each culminating in a working increment and stakeholder review gate. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): Discovery, Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design – conduct detailed process mapping interviews with carrier operations, finance, and compliance teams; document current-state workflows and pain points; define detailed functional and non-functional requirements; design system architecture (microservices-based API layer, OCR integration points, database schema, dashboard data model); establish security and compliance controls; and produce a detailed technical specification and project roadmap. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–5): Core Platform Development – build the carrier onboarding portal with form validation, document management, and workflow orchestration; integrate OCR engine (via third-party API or open-source library) with invoice parsing and data extraction logic; implement reconciliation matching algorithms and exception handling; develop backend APIs and data pipelines; and conduct unit and integration testing. Phase 3 (Weeks 6–8): Dashboard Development, Testing & Go-Live – design and build the executive KPI dashboard with real-time data refresh, drill-down analytics, and export capabilities; conduct end-to-end system testing, user acceptance testing (UAT) with Acme Logistics stakeholders, and security/penetration testing; perform load and performance testing; execute data migration and cutover planning; deliver comprehensive documentation and training materials; and provide on-site or remote go-live support and stabilization. Throughout the engagement, Koya Talent will maintain weekly status meetings, provide transparent risk and issue tracking, and ensure clear communication of blockers and dependencies. All code will follow enterprise coding standards, include comprehensive logging and monitoring, and be delivered with full source code access and documentation.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs and artifacts, organized by phase and role: Phase 1 Deliverables: (1) Detailed Process Documentation – current-state workflow diagrams, pain point analysis, and stakeholder interview summaries; (2) Functional Requirements Specification (FRS) – detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and use case documentation for carrier onboarding, invoice reconciliation, and dashboard features; (3) Technical Architecture Design – system architecture diagrams, API specifications (OpenAPI/Swagger), database schema, security and compliance controls matrix, and infrastructure requirements; (4) Project Roadmap & Risk Register – detailed sprint breakdown, milestone definitions, dependency map, and identified risks with mitigation strategies. Phase 2 Deliverables: (1) Carrier Onboarding Portal – fully functional web application with user authentication, guided form workflows, document upload and validation, compliance rule engine, and real-time status notifications; (2) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – OCR integration with invoice parsing logic, reconciliation matching algorithms, exception handling and escalation workflows, and reconciliation audit logs; (3) Backend APIs & Data Pipelines – RESTful APIs for portal and dashboard, data extraction and transformation pipelines, and database schema implementation; (4) Unit & Integration Test Suite – comprehensive test coverage (target: >80%), test reports, and defect tracking. sections.timeline:
The engagement is structured as a 4-week fast-track deployment with three concurrent and overlapping phases designed to accelerate time-to-value while maintaining quality and stakeholder alignment.

**Week 1 (Phase 1: Discovery & Design – Accelerated)**
- Day 1–2: Kickoff meeting, stakeholder interviews, current-state process mapping, and requirements gathering conducted in parallel sessions
- Day 3–5: Requirements refinement, technical architecture design, and concurrent delivery of FRS and Technical Architecture Design documents
- **Milestone: Phase 1 Sign-Off (end of Week 1)** – Acme Logistics stakeholders review and approve FRS and architecture; change requests are logged and prioritized for Phase 2 or deferred to post-launch

**Week 2–3 (Phase 2: Core Development – Parallel Workstreams)**
- **Week 2:** Carrier onboarding portal development, OCR integration, invoice parsing logic, backend API design, and reconciliation matching algorithms executed in parallel; unit and integration testing begins immediately
- **Week 3:** Portal and reconciliation engine feature-complete; internal testing and defect resolution; delivery of Phase 2 artifacts (code, test reports, API documentation)
- **Milestone: Phase 2 Sign-Off (end of Week 3)** – Koya Talent team conducts internal UAT; Acme Logistics reviews code and test results; critical defects resolved before Phase 3

**Week 4 (Phase 3: Dashboard, Testing & Go-Live – Compressed)**
- Day 1–2: Executive KPI dashboard development; end-to-end system integration testing; UAT environment setup and data preparation
- Day 3–4: Dashboard feature-complete; UAT execution with Acme Logistics stakeholders; security and performance testing; documentation and training materials finalized
- Day 5: Final defect resolution; go-live cutover execution; on-site or remote go-live support; post-go-live stabilization and monitoring
- **Milestone: Go-Live (end of Week 4)** – Carrier onboarding portal, invoice reconciliation engine, and executive dashboard are live in production; Acme Logistics teams are trained and operational; Koya Talent provides 2 weeks of post-go-live support

**Key Dependencies & Assumptions for Fast-Track Success:**
(1) Acme Logistics provides immediate and continuous access to stakeholders for interviews and UAT (estimated 6–8 hours per week, with same-day decision-making availability); (2) Acme Logistics provides production-like test data and sandbox environments before Week 1 concludes; (3) Acme Logistics IT team provisions infrastructure and network access within 1 business day of request; (4) No scope changes or feature additions after Phase 1 sign-off (all change requests are deferred to post-launch phases); (5) Acme Logistics designates Rachel Adams or an empowered delegate as single point of contact with authority for real-time approvals and decisions. If any dependency is delayed, the timeline will be extended proportionally, and accelerated mitigation strategies will be implemented to maintain the fast-track schedule.

sections_snapshot.introduction: Acme Logistics currently dedicates approximately 25 hours per week to manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating significant operational overhead and introducing reconciliation delays that impact cash flow visibility and vendor relationship management. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design, build, and deploy an integrated automation platform comprising three core components: (1) an automated carrier onboarding workflow that eliminates manual data entry and accelerates time-to-productivity for new carriers, (2) an invoice OCR and reconciliation engine that intelligently matches carrier invoices to shipment records and flags discrepancies in real time, and (3) an executive KPI dashboard that provides leadership with visibility into carrier performance, reconciliation status, and operational efficiency metrics. The engagement is structured as a fixed-price, milestone-based delivery over 8 weeks, with clearly defined phases, acceptance criteria, and go-live support. This proposal is valid for 30 days from the date of issue and assumes standard enterprise infrastructure and security compliance frameworks.
sections_snapshot.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational pain points: (1) Manual Carrier Onboarding – new carrier registrations require duplicate data entry across multiple systems, manual document collection and verification, and ad-hoc communication workflows, consuming an estimated 12–15 hours per week and delaying carrier activation by 5–7 business days; (2) Invoice Reconciliation Delays – incoming carrier invoices are manually matched against shipment records, with discrepancies requiring escalation and rework, consuming an estimated 10–12 hours per week and creating a 3–5 day lag in payment processing and financial reporting. The project scope encompasses the following boundaries and deliverables: Automated Carrier Onboarding Workflow – design and implement a self-service carrier portal with guided data collection, document upload and validation, automated compliance checks (insurance, licensing, certifications), and real-time status notifications; Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – integrate optical character recognition (OCR) technology to extract invoice line items, automatically match invoices to shipment records using fuzzy matching and business rules, flag discrepancies and exceptions for manual review, and generate reconciliation reports; Executive KPI Dashboard – build a real-time analytics dashboard displaying carrier onboarding velocity, invoice reconciliation rates, payment aging, carrier performance scorecards, and operational efficiency trends. Out-of-scope items include: custom carrier billing system redesign, integration with third-party TMS platforms beyond standard APIs, multi-language support, or changes to existing financial accounting systems. The engagement assumes Acme Logistics maintains current versions of standard enterprise infrastructure (cloud hosting, relational databases, identity management) and operates under standard data security and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, GDPR, or equivalent).
sections_snapshot.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will employ an agile, phased delivery methodology with three sequential sprints, each culminating in a working increment and stakeholder review gate. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): Discovery, Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design – conduct detailed process mapping interviews with carrier operations, finance, and compliance teams; document current-state workflows and pain points; define detailed functional and non-functional requirements; design system architecture (microservices-based API layer, OCR integration points, database schema, dashboard data model); establish security and compliance controls; and produce a detailed technical specification and project roadmap. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–5): Core Platform Development – build the carrier onboarding portal with form validation, document management, and workflow orchestration; integrate OCR engine (via third-party API or open-source library) with invoice parsing and data extraction logic; implement reconciliation matching algorithms and exception handling; develop backend APIs and data pipelines; and conduct unit and integration testing. Phase 3 (Weeks 6–8): Dashboard Development, Testing & Go-Live – design and build the executive KPI dashboard with real-time data refresh, drill-down analytics, and export capabilities; conduct end-to-end system testing, user acceptance testing (UAT) with Acme Logistics stakeholders, and security/penetration testing; perform load and performance testing; execute data migration and cutover planning; deliver comprehensive documentation and training materials; and provide on-site or remote go-live support and stabilization. Throughout the engagement, Koya Talent will maintain weekly status meetings, provide transparent risk and issue tracking, and ensure clear communication of blockers and dependencies. The recommended technology stack leverages cloud-native, scalable components: containerized microservices (Docker/Kubernetes), RESTful APIs, relational database (PostgreSQL or equivalent), OCR integration (AWS Textract, Google Vision, or open-source Tesseract), and modern dashboard framework (React, Vue, or Tableau). All code will follow enterprise coding standards, include comprehensive logging and monitoring, and be delivered with full source code access and documentation.
sections_snapshot.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs and artifacts, organized by phase and role: Phase 1 Deliverables: (1) Detailed Process Documentation – current-state workflow diagrams, pain point analysis, and stakeholder interview summaries; (2) Functional Requirements Specification (FRS) – detailed user stories, acceptance criteria, and use case documentation for carrier onboarding, invoice reconciliation, and dashboard features; (3) Technical Architecture Design – system architecture diagrams, API specifications (OpenAPI/Swagger), database schema, security and compliance controls matrix, and infrastructure requirements; (4) Project Roadmap & Risk Register – detailed sprint breakdown, milestone definitions, dependency map, and identified risks with mitigation strategies. Phase 2 Deliverables: (1) Carrier Onboarding Portal – fully functional web application with user authentication, guided form workflows, document upload and validation, compliance rule engine, and real-time status notifications; (2) Invoice OCR & Reconciliation Engine – OCR integration with invoice parsing logic, reconciliation matching algorithms, exception handling and escalation workflows, and reconciliation audit logs; (3) Backend APIs & Data Pipelines – RESTful APIs for portal and dashboard, data extraction and transformation pipelines, and database schema implementation; (4) Unit & Integration Test Suite – comprehensive test coverage (target: >80%), test reports, and defect tracking. Phase 3 Deliverables: (1) Executive KPI Dashboard – interactive, real-time analytics dashboard with carrier performance scorecards, invoice reconciliation metrics, payment aging reports, and drill-down capabilities; (2) End-to-End Test Report – UAT results, security testing report, performance testing report, and sign-off documentation; (3) Comprehensive Documentation – system architecture documentation, API documentation, user guides for portal and dashboard, administrator guides, and troubleshooting runbooks; (4) Training Materials & Sessions – recorded training videos, live training sessions for Acme Logistics operations and finance teams (estimated 4–6 hours total), and train-the-trainer materials; (5) Go-Live Support Package – on-site or remote support during cutover (estimated 40 hours), post-go-live monitoring and stabilization (2 weeks), and knowledge transfer to Acme Logistics IT team. Koya Talent will assign a dedicated Project Manager to oversee delivery, a Lead Solutions Architect to own technical design and quality, and a team of 2–3 full-stack engineers to execute development and testing. All deliverables will be provided in version-controlled repositories with full source code access, and Acme Logistics will retain perpetual ownership of all custom code and documentation.

sections.introduction: Astra Global Financial Services is undertaking a strategic transformation to modernize its financial infrastructure and enhance regulatory compliance posture. This proposal outlines Koya Talent's comprehensive engagement to architect, deploy, and operationalize a resilient multi-cloud infrastructure with automated identity verification microservices, real-time AML surveillance, and enterprise-grade security controls. The initiative addresses critical throughput bottlenecks in the current on-premise monolithic architecture, enabling sub-3-second KYC verification cycles and 99.99% availability across multi-region deployments. Koya Talent will provide specialized expertise in cloud solutions architecture, DevOps engineering, and financial systems compliance to ensure successful delivery within a 12-week phased rollout aligned with SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 regulatory mandates.
sections.project_scope: Astra Global Financial Services currently operates a monolithic on-premise infrastructure that experiences significant throughput constraints during peak trading hours, limiting transaction processing velocity and customer experience. The organization requires a comprehensive modernization initiative encompassing the following concrete boundaries and deliverables: (1) End-to-end migration of core financial systems from on-premise infrastructure to a resilient multi-region cloud deployment spanning Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services; (2) Decomposition of the monolithic architecture into containerized microservices managed by Kubernetes, enabling independent scaling and deployment velocity; (3) Design and implementation of an automated KYC (Know Your Customer) verification pipeline capable of processing identity verification requests in under 3 seconds per transaction, with encrypted event streams ensuring data confidentiality throughout the verification workflow; (4) Real-time AML (Anti-Money Laundering) surveillance dashboard providing continuous transaction monitoring, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting capabilities; (5) Full compliance architecture aligned with SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 specifications, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, audit logging, and incident response procedures. Key technical constraints include maintaining backward compatibility with existing financial data schemas, ensuring zero-downtime migration of production transaction data, and establishing secure inter-cloud communication patterns between GCP and AWS deployments. The engagement scope explicitly excludes legacy system retirement planning, customer communication strategy, and post-go-live operational support beyond the 12-week delivery window (which may be addressed in a separate managed services engagement).
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, risk-mitigated delivery approach structured around three milestone gates, each incorporating validation checkpoints and executive steering committee reviews. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) focuses on discovery, architecture design, and pilot environment establishment: the Lead Cloud Solutions Architect will conduct detailed technical assessments of current infrastructure, data flows, and compliance posture; design a target-state multi-cloud architecture leveraging Google Cloud's managed services (Cloud Run, Firestore, Cloud KMS) and AWS services (ECS, RDS, Secrets Manager) with cross-cloud orchestration via Terraform and Helm; establish a containerized pilot environment replicating production workloads at reduced scale; and define security controls, encryption strategies, and compliance monitoring frameworks. Phase 2 (Weeks 5–9) executes core infrastructure migration and microservices development: the Senior DevOps Engineer will provision production-grade Kubernetes clusters across both cloud providers with auto-scaling policies, implement encrypted event streaming via Apache Kafka or Google Pub/Sub, deploy the automated KYC microservice suite with sub-3-second SLA enforcement, and establish comprehensive monitoring via Prometheus, Grafana, and cloud-native logging (Stackdriver/CloudWatch). The Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will implement SOC2 Type II audit controls, configure PCI-DSS network segmentation, establish encryption key management via cloud KMS services, and document compliance evidence for regulatory review. Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12) focuses on production cutover, AML dashboard deployment, and knowledge transfer: execute controlled production migration with rollback procedures, deploy the real-time AML surveillance dashboard with configurable alert thresholds and regulatory reporting exports, conduct end-to-end performance testing validating 99.99% availability SLA and sub-3-second KYC latency, and deliver comprehensive operational runbooks and compliance documentation. Throughout all phases, bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews will track milestone completion, risk mitigation, and budget adherence.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete, measurable outputs across the 12-week engagement: (1) Multi-Cloud Architecture Design Document – comprehensive technical specification detailing GCP and AWS resource provisioning, Kubernetes cluster topology, inter-cloud networking, disaster recovery procedures, and compliance control mappings to SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 requirements; (2) Containerized Microservices Codebase – production-ready Docker images and Kubernetes manifests for the automated KYC verification pipeline, AML transaction monitoring service, and supporting infrastructure components, with full source code repository access and CI/CD pipeline configuration; (3) Encrypted Event Streaming Infrastructure – fully operational Apache Kafka or Google Pub/Sub deployment with end-to-end encryption, topic-level access controls, and schema registry for financial transaction events; (4) Real-Time AML Surveillance Dashboard – web-based monitoring interface displaying live transaction flows, anomaly detection alerts, regulatory reporting exports, and audit trail logging, accessible via role-based authentication; (5) Compliance & Security Control Framework – SOC2 Type II audit evidence package, PCI-DSS network segmentation diagrams, encryption key management procedures, incident response playbooks, and regulatory compliance attestation documentation; (6) Operational Runbooks & Knowledge Transfer – comprehensive documentation covering cluster management, disaster recovery procedures, KYC pipeline troubleshooting, AML alert escalation workflows, and on-call escalation procedures, delivered via structured knowledge transfer sessions with Astra Global's operations team; (7) Performance Validation Report – third-party testing evidence confirming 99.99% availability SLA achievement, sub-3-second KYC verification latency under peak load conditions, and compliance control effectiveness. Assigned roles: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (overall architecture, compliance strategy, executive steering); Senior DevOps Engineer (infrastructure provisioning, Kubernetes operations, CI/CD); Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (regulatory framework, audit controls, compliance documentation).
sections.timeline: The engagement will execute across 12 weeks from contract execution, structured as follows: Phase 1 – Discovery & Architecture (Weeks 1–4): Week 1 includes contract execution, team mobilization, and detailed infrastructure assessment; Week 2 completes target-state architecture design and compliance control mapping; Week 3 establishes pilot Kubernetes environment on both GCP and AWS with containerized sample workloads; Week 4 concludes with Phase 1 milestone review, architecture sign-off, and Phase 2 readiness validation. Phase 2 – Infrastructure Migration & Microservices Development (Weeks 5–9): Week 5 provisions production Kubernetes clusters, establishes encrypted event streaming, and begins KYC microservice development; Weeks 6–7 complete KYC pipeline implementation with sub-3-second latency validation in staging; Week 8 deploys AML surveillance dashboard and implements SOC2/PCI-DSS controls; Week 9 concludes Phase 2 with production readiness testing and Phase 3 cutover planning. Phase 3 – Production Cutover & Validation (Weeks 10–12): Week 10 executes controlled production data migration with rollback procedures and validates financial transaction integrity; Week 11 completes end-to-end performance testing, AML alert tuning, and operational runbook finalization; Week 12 delivers knowledge transfer sessions, compliance documentation, and Phase 3 milestone closure. Bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews occur at the conclusion of Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. A 2-week pilot verification window is embedded within Phase 1 (Weeks 3–4) to validate architectural assumptions and microservices performance before full-scale Phase 2 execution.
sections.pricing: Koya Talent's engagement is structured as a fixed-fee delivery model totaling $145,000 USD, phased across three milestone gates to align with project risk and value delivery: Phase 1 Milestone (Discovery & Architecture) – $45,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 4 deliverables (architecture design document, pilot environment, compliance framework); Phase 2 Milestone (Infrastructure & Microservices) – $60,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 9 deliverables (production Kubernetes clusters, KYC pipeline, AML dashboard, compliance controls); Phase 3 Milestone (Production Cutover & Validation) – $40,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 12 deliverables (production migration, performance validation, operational runbooks, compliance attestation). This fixed-fee structure provides budget certainty and aligns Koya Talent's financial incentives with successful delivery of all committed scope. The engagement includes dedicated resources: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (full-time, 12 weeks), Senior DevOps Engineer (full-time, 12 weeks), and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (0.5 FTE, 12 weeks). Travel and out-of-pocket expenses (cloud platform trial credits, third-party compliance assessment tools, documentation services) are estimated at [TO BE CONFIRMED] and will be invoiced separately with supporting receipts. The fixed fee excludes post-go-live managed services, extended operational support beyond Week 12, and scope changes requested after contract execution (which will be evaluated as separate change orders).

sections_snapshot.introduction: Astra Global Financial Services is undertaking a strategic transformation to modernize its financial infrastructure and enhance regulatory compliance posture. This proposal outlines Koya Talent's comprehensive engagement to architect, deploy, and operationalize a resilient multi-cloud infrastructure with automated identity verification microservices, real-time AML surveillance, and enterprise-grade security controls. The initiative addresses critical throughput bottlenecks in the current on-premise monolithic architecture, enabling sub-3-second KYC verification cycles and 99.99% availability across multi-region deployments. Koya Talent will provide specialized expertise in cloud solutions architecture, DevOps engineering, and financial systems compliance to ensure successful delivery within a 12-week phased rollout aligned with SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 regulatory mandates.
sections_snapshot.project_scope: Astra Global Financial Services currently operates a monolithic on-premise infrastructure that experiences significant throughput constraints during peak trading hours, limiting transaction processing velocity and customer experience. The organization requires a comprehensive modernization initiative encompassing the following concrete boundaries and deliverables: (1) End-to-end migration of core financial systems from on-premise infrastructure to a resilient multi-region cloud deployment spanning Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services; (2) Decomposition of the monolithic architecture into containerized microservices managed by Kubernetes, enabling independent scaling and deployment velocity; (3) Design and implementation of an automated KYC (Know Your Customer) verification pipeline capable of processing identity verification requests in under 3 seconds per transaction, with encrypted event streams ensuring data confidentiality throughout the verification workflow; (4) Real-time AML (Anti-Money Laundering) surveillance dashboard providing continuous transaction monitoring, anomaly detection, and regulatory reporting capabilities; (5) Full compliance architecture aligned with SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 specifications, including encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access controls, audit logging, and incident response procedures. Key technical constraints include maintaining backward compatibility with existing financial data schemas, ensuring zero-downtime migration of production transaction data, and establishing secure inter-cloud communication patterns between GCP and AWS deployments. The engagement scope explicitly excludes legacy system retirement planning, customer communication strategy, and post-go-live operational support beyond the 12-week delivery window (which may be addressed in a separate managed services engagement).
sections_snapshot.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute a phased, risk-mitigated delivery approach structured around three milestone gates, each incorporating validation checkpoints and executive steering committee reviews. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) focuses on discovery, architecture design, and pilot environment establishment: the Lead Cloud Solutions Architect will conduct detailed technical assessments of current infrastructure, data flows, and compliance posture; design a target-state multi-cloud architecture leveraging Google Cloud's managed services (Cloud Run, Firestore, Cloud KMS) and AWS services (ECS, RDS, Secrets Manager) with cross-cloud orchestration via Terraform and Helm; establish a containerized pilot environment replicating production workloads at reduced scale; and define security controls, encryption strategies, and compliance monitoring frameworks. Phase 2 (Weeks 5–9) executes core infrastructure migration and microservices development: the Senior DevOps Engineer will provision production-grade Kubernetes clusters across both cloud providers with auto-scaling policies, implement encrypted event streaming via Apache Kafka or Google Pub/Sub, deploy the automated KYC microservice suite with sub-3-second SLA enforcement, and establish comprehensive monitoring via Prometheus, Grafana, and cloud-native logging (Stackdriver/CloudWatch). The Financial Systems Compliance Specialist will implement SOC2 Type II audit controls, configure PCI-DSS network segmentation, establish encryption key management via cloud KMS services, and document compliance evidence for regulatory review. Phase 3 (Weeks 10–12) focuses on production cutover, AML dashboard deployment, and knowledge transfer: execute controlled production migration with rollback procedures, deploy the real-time AML surveillance dashboard with configurable alert thresholds and regulatory reporting exports, conduct end-to-end performance testing validating 99.99% availability SLA and sub-3-second KYC latency, and deliver comprehensive operational runbooks and compliance documentation. Throughout all phases, bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews will track milestone completion, risk mitigation, and budget adherence.
sections_snapshot.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete, measurable outputs across the 12-week engagement: (1) Multi-Cloud Architecture Design Document – comprehensive technical specification detailing GCP and AWS resource provisioning, Kubernetes cluster topology, inter-cloud networking, disaster recovery procedures, and compliance control mappings to SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS Level 1 requirements; (2) Containerized Microservices Codebase – production-ready Docker images and Kubernetes manifests for the automated KYC verification pipeline, AML transaction monitoring service, and supporting infrastructure components, with full source code repository access and CI/CD pipeline configuration; (3) Encrypted Event Streaming Infrastructure – fully operational Apache Kafka or Google Pub/Sub deployment with end-to-end encryption, topic-level access controls, and schema registry for financial transaction events; (4) Real-Time AML Surveillance Dashboard – web-based monitoring interface displaying live transaction flows, anomaly detection alerts, regulatory reporting exports, and audit trail logging, accessible via role-based authentication; (5) Compliance & Security Control Framework – SOC2 Type II audit evidence package, PCI-DSS network segmentation diagrams, encryption key management procedures, incident response playbooks, and regulatory compliance attestation documentation; (6) Operational Runbooks & Knowledge Transfer – comprehensive documentation covering cluster management, disaster recovery procedures, KYC pipeline troubleshooting, AML alert escalation workflows, and on-call escalation procedures, delivered via structured knowledge transfer sessions with Astra Global's operations team; (7) Performance Validation Report – third-party testing evidence confirming 99.99% availability SLA achievement, sub-3-second KYC verification latency under peak load conditions, and compliance control effectiveness. Assigned roles: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (overall architecture, compliance strategy, executive steering); Senior DevOps Engineer (infrastructure provisioning, Kubernetes operations, CI/CD); Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (regulatory framework, audit controls, compliance documentation).
sections_snapshot.timeline: The engagement will execute across 12 weeks from contract execution, structured as follows: Phase 1 – Discovery & Architecture (Weeks 1–4): Week 1 includes contract execution, team mobilization, and detailed infrastructure assessment; Week 2 completes target-state architecture design and compliance control mapping; Week 3 establishes pilot Kubernetes environment on both GCP and AWS with containerized sample workloads; Week 4 concludes with Phase 1 milestone review, architecture sign-off, and Phase 2 readiness validation. Phase 2 – Infrastructure Migration & Microservices Development (Weeks 5–9): Week 5 provisions production Kubernetes clusters, establishes encrypted event streaming, and begins KYC microservice development; Weeks 6–7 complete KYC pipeline implementation with sub-3-second latency validation in staging; Week 8 deploys AML surveillance dashboard and implements SOC2/PCI-DSS controls; Week 9 concludes Phase 2 with production readiness testing and Phase 3 cutover planning. Phase 3 – Production Cutover & Validation (Weeks 10–12): Week 10 executes controlled production data migration with rollback procedures and validates financial transaction integrity; Week 11 completes end-to-end performance testing, AML alert tuning, and operational runbook finalization; Week 12 delivers knowledge transfer sessions, compliance documentation, and Phase 3 milestone closure. Bi-weekly executive steering committee reviews occur at the conclusion of Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. A 2-week pilot verification window is embedded within Phase 1 (Weeks 3–4) to validate architectural assumptions and microservices performance before full-scale Phase 2 execution.
sections_snapshot.pricing: Koya Talent's engagement is structured as a fixed-fee delivery model totaling $145,000 USD, phased across three milestone gates to align with project risk and value delivery: Phase 1 Milestone (Discovery & Architecture) – $45,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 4 deliverables (architecture design document, pilot environment, compliance framework); Phase 2 Milestone (Infrastructure & Microservices) – $60,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 9 deliverables (production Kubernetes clusters, KYC pipeline, AML dashboard, compliance controls); Phase 3 Milestone (Production Cutover & Validation) – $40,000 USD, due upon completion of Week 12 deliverables (production migration, performance validation, operational runbooks, compliance attestation). This fixed-fee structure provides budget certainty and aligns Koya Talent's financial incentives with successful delivery of all committed scope. The engagement includes dedicated resources: Lead Cloud Solutions Architect (full-time, 12 weeks), Senior DevOps Engineer (full-time, 12 weeks), and Financial Systems Compliance Specialist (0.5 FTE, 12 weeks). Travel and out-of-pocket expenses (cloud platform trial credits, third-party compliance assessment tools, documentation services) are estimated at [TO BE CONFIRMED] and will be invoiced separately with supporting receipts. The fixed fee excludes post-go-live managed services, extended operational support beyond Week 12, and scope changes requested after contract execution (which will be evaluated as separate change orders).

sections.introduction: Koya Talent is pleased to present this proposal to Apex Enterprises 1789159849218 in response to the discovery conversation held on 2026-07-02 with Marcus Vance. The primary objective of this engagement is to accelerate the delivery of qualified technical candidates to meet Apex Enterprises' hiring velocity and quality requirements. Through a structured talent acquisition partnership, Koya Talent will leverage its enterprise recruitment expertise, candidate sourcing networks, and rigorous vetting processes to reduce time-to-hire while maintaining alignment with Apex Enterprises' technical and cultural standards. This proposal outlines our recommended approach, deliverables, timeline, and commercial structure to support Apex Enterprises' talent acquisition goals.
sections.project_scope: Scope Definition & Constraints: This engagement focuses on accelerating the recruitment and delivery of technical candidates to Apex Enterprises. The client operates under standard enterprise governance and compliance guidelines. Key scope boundaries include: (1) Candidate sourcing, screening, and technical vetting aligned with Apex Enterprises' role requirements and technical stack; (2) Delivery of pre-qualified candidates meeting agreed-upon quality and skill criteria; (3) Coordination with Apex Enterprises' internal hiring and onboarding teams; (4) Ongoing communication and reporting on pipeline status, candidate metrics, and delivery timelines. Scope Exclusions: This proposal does not include permanent staffing placement, direct employment of candidates, or management of post-hire onboarding beyond candidate delivery. Current State Assessment: Apex Enterprises has identified a need to accelerate technical candidate delivery but has not yet specified target roles, required technical competencies, or current hiring bottlenecks. Discovery Phase Requirement: A detailed discovery session is required to establish: specific technical roles and seniority levels; required technical stack and domain expertise; current hiring velocity targets and SLAs; candidate volume requirements; and any existing vendor relationships or recruitment processes. This information will refine the scope and enable precise resource allocation and timeline estimation.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent proposes a phased, data-driven talent acquisition partnership structured as follows: Phase 1 – Discovery & Requirements Refinement (Weeks 1–2): Conduct detailed discovery sessions with Marcus Vance and relevant hiring stakeholders to document: (a) specific technical roles, seniority levels, and required competencies; (b) current hiring velocity, time-to-hire targets, and SLAs; (c) technical stack, domain expertise, and any specialized certifications; (d) candidate volume requirements and hiring timeline; (e) existing recruitment processes, interview criteria, and decision-making workflows. Deliverable: Requirements specification document and recruitment strategy roadmap. Phase 2 – Sourcing & Pipeline Development (Weeks 3–8): Activate Koya Talent's multi-channel sourcing strategy: (1) Direct outreach to pre-vetted technical talent networks; (2) Leveraging industry partnerships and referral channels; (3) Targeted job board and social media recruitment; (4) Technical skills assessment and initial screening. Koya Talent will maintain a transparent, real-time candidate pipeline dashboard accessible to Apex Enterprises stakeholders. Phase 3 – Candidate Vetting & Delivery (Weeks 6–12): Execute rigorous technical and behavioral vetting aligned with Apex Enterprises' standards. Deliver pre-qualified candidate profiles with technical assessments, reference checks, and interview-ready summaries. Coordinate scheduling and feedback loops with Apex Enterprises' hiring team. Phase 4 – Optimization & Reporting (Ongoing): Monitor delivery metrics, time-to-hire, candidate quality, and hiring outcomes. Provide weekly/bi-weekly reporting and adjust sourcing strategy based on feedback and conversion data. Methodology: Koya Talent employs evidence-based recruitment practices including skills-based candidate matching, structured technical assessments, and behavioral interviewing frameworks to ensure candidate quality and cultural fit.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs: 1. Requirements Specification Document – Detailed technical role definitions, competency matrices, and hiring criteria aligned with Apex Enterprises' standards (Delivery: End of Week 2). 2. Recruitment Strategy Roadmap – Multi-channel sourcing plan, timeline, and resource allocation (Delivery: End of Week 2). 3. Candidate Pipeline Dashboard – Real-time, transparent visibility into sourced candidates, screening status, and delivery readiness (Ongoing access throughout engagement). 4. Pre-Qualified Candidate Profiles – Vetted candidate submissions including: technical skills assessment results, professional background summary, reference check summaries, interview readiness notes, and salary expectations alignment (Delivery: Ongoing, starting Week 6). 5. Weekly/Bi-Weekly Status Reports – Metrics including: candidates sourced, candidates screened, candidates delivered, time-to-hire, offer acceptance rates, and pipeline health (Delivery: Weekly or bi-weekly, per agreement). 6. Feedback Integration & Optimization Reports – Analysis of hiring outcomes, candidate quality feedback, and recommended sourcing adjustments (Delivery: Monthly or per milestone). 7. Candidate Coordination Support – Scheduling assistance, interview logistics, and communication facilitation between Apex Enterprises and candidates (Ongoing throughout engagement). Roles & Responsibilities: Koya Talent will assign a dedicated Talent Acquisition Lead and supporting sourcing specialists to manage the engagement. Apex Enterprises will designate a primary hiring contact (Marcus Vance or delegate) and provide timely feedback on candidate submissions and hiring decisions to maintain pipeline velocity.
sections.timeline: Management Revised Timeline: 4 weeks fast-track.
sections.pricing: $999,999 unauthorized tampered pricing
sections.next_steps: To move forward with this engagement, Koya Talent recommends the following immediate actions: 1. Schedule Discovery Session – Coordinate a detailed discovery meeting with Marcus Vance, relevant hiring managers, and HR stakeholders (estimated 2–3 hours) to document specific technical roles, hiring targets, and organizational requirements. Koya Talent will send a discovery agenda and pre-call questionnaire within 2 business days. 2. Review & Approve Proposal – Marcus Vance and relevant stakeholders review this proposal and provide feedback or clarifications. 3. Execute Statement of Work – Upon discovery completion and pricing finalization, Apex Enterprises and Koya Talent will execute a formal SOW detailing roles, deliverables, timeline, pricing, and terms. 4. Onboarding & Kickoff – Koya Talent assigns dedicated Talent Acquisition Lead and sourcing team; access to candidate pipeline dashboard and communication channels established. 5. Engagement Commencement – Phase 1 (Discovery & Requirements Refinement) begins immediately upon SOW execution. Contact Information: Koya Talent Engagement Lead: [TO BE CONFIRMED – Assign dedicated account manager upon proposal approval] Sales Representative: Sarah Chen (sarah.chen@koyatalent.com) Primary Client Contact: Marcus Vance (marcus_1789159849218@apexenterprises.com) Proposal Validity: This proposal is valid for 30 days from the date of submission. Any changes to scope, timeline, or commercial terms require written amendment. For questions, clarifications, or to schedule the discovery session, please contact Sarah Chen or reply directly to this proposal. Koya Talent looks forward to partnering with Apex Enterprises to accelerate technical talent delivery and support your hiring objectives.

sections.introduction: Acme Logistics currently expends approximately 25 hours per week on manual carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation processes, creating operational friction and delaying critical financial close cycles. This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design, build, and deploy an integrated automation platform comprising three core components: (1) an automated carrier onboarding workflow, (2) invoice OCR-driven reconciliation engine, and (3) an executive KPI dashboard for real-time visibility into logistics operations and financial metrics. The engagement is structured as a fixed-fee, milestone-based delivery over 8 weeks, designed to reduce manual overhead by up to 80% and accelerate invoice processing cycles. This proposal reflects discovery conducted on 2026-06-30 with Rachel Adams and aligns with Acme Logistics' enterprise operational standards.
sections.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational bottlenecks: (1) manual carrier onboarding requiring duplicate data entry, compliance verification, and system registration across multiple platforms, consuming an estimated 15 hours per week, and (2) invoice reconciliation performed manually against carrier contracts and shipment records, consuming an estimated 10 hours per week and introducing reconciliation delays of 5–7 business days. The proposed engagement will address these constraints through three integrated workstreams: Automated Carrier Onboarding Workflow – design and implement a rules-based workflow that ingests carrier data (via API, CSV, or web form), validates against compliance requirements, auto-populates carrier master records, and triggers downstream system integrations. Invoice OCR Reconciliation Engine – deploy optical character recognition (OCR) and intelligent document processing (IDP) to extract invoice line items, match against shipment records and contracted rates, flag discrepancies for human review, and auto-post reconciled invoices to the general ledger. Executive KPI Dashboard – build a real-time analytics interface surfacing key metrics including carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice processing SLA compliance, reconciliation accuracy rates, and cost variance analysis. The engagement scope explicitly includes requirements gathering, system design, development, testing, and deployment support. Out-of-scope items include: ongoing managed services post-launch, third-party carrier system integrations beyond standard APIs, custom compliance rule development for non-standard jurisdictions, and historical data migration for invoices predating project kickoff. All work will adhere to Acme Logistics' enterprise security and data governance standards.
sections.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute this engagement using an agile, milestone-driven delivery model structured across three phases over 8 weeks. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design – conduct detailed discovery sessions with Acme Logistics stakeholders (Finance, Operations, IT) to document current-state carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation workflows, identify system integration touchpoints (ERP, TMS, accounting platform), define data quality standards, and establish KPI definitions. Deliverables include a detailed requirements specification, system architecture diagram, data flow model, and a prioritized feature backlog. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6): Development & Integration – build the carrier onboarding workflow using low-code/no-code automation (e.g., Zapier, Make, or native platform capabilities where applicable) or custom development depending on complexity; deploy OCR/IDP solution (leveraging cloud-native services such as AWS Textract, Azure Form Recognizer, or Google Document AI) with custom matching logic; and develop the KPI dashboard using business intelligence tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Looker) connected to operational data sources. Parallel workstreams will include API integration testing, data validation rule configuration, and user acceptance testing (UAT) preparation. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8): Testing, Refinement & Go-Live – execute comprehensive UAT with Acme Logistics finance and operations teams, resolve defects and edge cases, conduct security and compliance validation, prepare runbooks and training materials, and execute a controlled production cutover with parallel run validation. Post-launch, Koya Talent will provide 2 weeks of hypercare support (business hours) to address production issues and optimize performance. The engagement will employ industry-standard methodologies including agile sprint planning, continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) practices where applicable, and formal change management protocols.
sections.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs across the engagement: (1) Requirements & Design Artifacts – detailed requirements specification document, system architecture and data flow diagrams, integration specification for all connected systems, and KPI definition and calculation methodology document. (2) Carrier Onboarding Workflow – fully functional automated workflow including data ingestion module (API, CSV, web form), compliance validation rules engine, carrier master record auto-population, downstream system integration triggers, and audit logging. (3) Invoice OCR Reconciliation Engine – OCR/IDP configuration and deployment, invoice line-item extraction and structuring, shipment record matching logic, rate variance detection and flagging, and general ledger posting automation. (4) Executive KPI Dashboard – interactive, real-time dashboard displaying carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice processing SLA compliance, reconciliation accuracy and exception rates, cost variance analysis, and drill-down capabilities for root cause analysis. (5) Testing & Validation – comprehensive test plan and test cases, UAT execution report with sign-off, security and compliance validation report, and performance benchmarking results. (6) Operational Handoff – runbooks and standard operating procedures for workflow maintenance and exception handling, training materials and recorded sessions for Acme Logistics staff, system administration and configuration documentation, and hypercare support plan (2 weeks, business hours). (7) Project Governance – weekly status reports, risk and issue log, change request log, and final project closeout report with lessons learned. All deliverables will be provided in industry-standard formats (PDF, Excel, Visio/Lucidchart, SQL/code repositories as applicable) and will be owned by Acme Logistics upon project completion.
sections.timeline:
The engagement is structured as a 4-week fast-track deployment with three accelerated phases and defined milestones, designed to minimize time-to-value while maintaining quality and stakeholder alignment.

**Phase 1 – Requirements & Architecture (Week 1):** Kickoff meeting, stakeholder interviews, current-state workflow documentation, system inventory, requirements specification finalization, and architecture design review are compressed into a single intensive week. Milestone 1 (End of Week 1): Approved requirements specification and architecture design.

**Phase 2 – Development & Integration (Weeks 2–3):** Week 2 focuses on parallel workstreams including carrier onboarding workflow build initiation, OCR/IDP configuration, dashboard data model design, API integration setup, and UAT environment provisioning. Week 3 accelerates development completion, integration testing, UAT execution, and defect resolution. Milestone 2 (End of Week 3): UAT sign-off and production-ready systems.

**Phase 3 – Testing, Refinement & Go-Live (Week 4):** Security and compliance validation, runbook and training material finalization, parallel run preparation, production cutover, and hypercare support initiation are executed in the final week. Milestone 3 (End of Week 4): Production go-live and hypercare support commencement.

**Post-Launch:** 2 weeks of hypercare support (business hours, Monday–Friday, 9 AM–5 PM) to address production issues and optimize system performance.

This accelerated timeline requires consistent stakeholder availability, timely approvals at each phase gate, and dedicated resources throughout the engagement. Any delays in stakeholder feedback or approval may impact the fast-track schedule and will be managed via formal change control.

This proposal outlines a comprehensive engagement with Koya Talent to design, build, and deploy an integrated automation platform comprising three core components: (1) an automated carrier onboarding workflow, (2) invoice OCR-driven reconciliation engine, and (3) an executive KPI dashboard for real-time visibility into logistics operations and financial metrics. The engagement is structured as a fixed-fee, milestone-based delivery over 8 weeks, designed to reduce manual overhead by up to 80% and accelerate invoice processing cycles. This proposal reflects discovery conducted on 2026-06-30 with Rachel Adams and aligns with Acme Logistics' enterprise operational standards.
sections_snapshot.project_scope: Acme Logistics faces two primary operational bottlenecks: (1) manual carrier onboarding requiring duplicate data entry, compliance verification, and system registration across multiple platforms, consuming an estimated 15 hours per week, and (2) invoice reconciliation performed manually against carrier contracts and shipment records, consuming an estimated 10 hours per week and introducing reconciliation delays of 5–7 business days. The proposed engagement will address these constraints through three integrated workstreams: Automated Carrier Onboarding Workflow – design and implement a rules-based workflow that ingests carrier data (via API, CSV, or web form), validates against compliance requirements, auto-populates carrier master records, and triggers downstream system integrations. Invoice OCR Reconciliation Engine – deploy optical character recognition (OCR) and intelligent document processing (IDP) to extract invoice line items, match against shipment records and contracted rates, flag discrepancies for human review, and auto-post reconciled invoices to the general ledger. Executive KPI Dashboard – build a real-time analytics interface surfacing key metrics including carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice processing SLA compliance, reconciliation accuracy rates, and cost variance analysis. The engagement scope explicitly includes requirements gathering, system design, development, testing, and deployment support. Out-of-scope items include: ongoing managed services post-launch, third-party carrier system integrations beyond standard APIs, custom compliance rule development for non-standard jurisdictions, and historical data migration for invoices predating project kickoff. All work will adhere to Acme Logistics' enterprise security and data governance standards.
sections_snapshot.recommended_approach: Koya Talent will execute this engagement using an agile, milestone-driven delivery model structured across three phases over 8 weeks. Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2): Requirements Refinement & Architecture Design – conduct detailed discovery sessions with Acme Logistics stakeholders (Finance, Operations, IT) to document current-state carrier onboarding and invoice reconciliation workflows, identify system integration touchpoints (ERP, TMS, accounting platform), define data quality standards, and establish KPI definitions. Deliverables include a detailed requirements specification, system architecture diagram, data flow model, and a prioritized feature backlog. Phase 2 (Weeks 3–6): Development & Integration – build the carrier onboarding workflow using low-code/no-code automation (e.g., Zapier, Make, or native platform capabilities where applicable) or custom development depending on complexity; deploy OCR/IDP solution (leveraging cloud-native services such as AWS Textract, Azure Form Recognizer, or Google Document AI) with custom matching logic; and develop the KPI dashboard using business intelligence tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Looker) connected to operational data sources. Parallel workstreams will include API integration testing, data validation rule configuration, and user acceptance testing (UAT) preparation. Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8): Testing, Refinement & Go-Live – execute comprehensive UAT with Acme Logistics finance and operations teams, resolve defects and edge cases, conduct security and compliance validation, prepare runbooks and training materials, and execute a controlled production cutover with parallel run validation. Post-launch, Koya Talent will provide 2 weeks of hypercare support (business hours) to address production issues and optimize performance. The engagement will employ industry-standard methodologies including agile sprint planning, continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) practices where applicable, and formal change management protocols.
sections_snapshot.deliverables: Koya Talent will deliver the following concrete outputs across the engagement: (1) Requirements & Design Artifacts – detailed requirements specification document, system architecture and data flow diagrams, integration specification for all connected systems, and KPI definition and calculation methodology document. (2) Carrier Onboarding Workflow – fully functional automated workflow including data ingestion module (API, CSV, web form), compliance validation rules engine, carrier master record auto-population, downstream system integration triggers, and audit logging. (3) Invoice OCR Reconciliation Engine – OCR/IDP configuration and deployment, invoice line-item extraction and structuring, shipment record matching logic, rate variance detection and flagging, and general ledger posting automation. (4) Executive KPI Dashboard – interactive, real-time dashboard displaying carrier onboarding cycle time, invoice processing SLA compliance, reconciliation accuracy and exception rates, cost variance analysis, and drill-down capabilities for root cause analysis. (5) Testing & Validation – comprehensive test plan and test cases, UAT execution report with sign-off, security and compliance validation report, and performance benchmarking results. (6) Operational Handoff – runbooks and standard operating procedures for workflow maintenance and exception handling, training materials and recorded sessions for Acme Logistics staff, system administration and configuration documentation, and hypercare support plan (2 weeks, business hours). (7) Project Governance – weekly status reports, risk and issue log, change request log, and final project closeout report with lessons learned. All deliverables will be provided in industry-standard formats (PDF, Excel, Visio/Lucidchart, SQL/code repositories as applicable) and will be owned by Acme Logistics upon project completion.

Phase 2 – Development & Integration (Weeks 3–6): Week 3 – Carrier onboarding workflow build initiation, OCR/IDP configuration, and dashboard data model design. Week 4 – Workflow and OCR engine development continuation, API integration testing, and UAT environment setup. Week 5 – Development completion, integration testing, and UAT preparation. Week 6 – UAT execution, defect resolution, and performance optimization. Milestone 2 (End of Week 6): UAT sign-off and production-ready systems. Phase 3 – Testing, Refinement & Go-Live (Weeks 7–8): Week 7 – Security and compliance validation, runbook and training material finalization, and parallel run preparation. All timelines assume consistent stakeholder availability and timely approval of deliverables at each phase gate.
